It starts with a short, time-boxed documentation phase (design brief, content inventory, wireframes, tokens, motion spec, architecture) because no code is written until the big decisions have written answers. A deployed, themed, budgeted skeleton then proves hosting, CI, theming and reduced-motion handling before anything is built on top. Next comes a content-complete site with navigation, resume and copy-email, so the recruiter fast path works before any motion is layered on. The motion system and the signature project rail (reference 539: hover/lift on desktop, swipe and tap on touch, focused overlay) come after that. The rail is the first real use of the animation layer, and the phase ends with measured keep-or-drop decisions on react-spring and LazyMotion. Section treatments (experience cards, skills slider, education card, hero text effect) follow. Two React contexts exist (motion preference and, via the DOM, theme).\n72\t\n73\t**Key Characteristics:**\n74\t- Static output only: `npm run build` produces `dist/`; no runtime server or API calls.\n75\t- The DOM is the source of truth for theme: `html[data-theme]` is read by `readTheme()` and written by `applyTheme()` and the pre-paint script in `index.html`.\n76\t- Animation is isolated behind one barrel (`src/anim/index.ts`). Lint rules enforce that sections and layout never import `motion` or `@react-spring/web` directly (`.oxlintrc.json`).\n77\t- Static HTML in `index.html` mirrors the rendered Hero and section headings so content exists before JavaScript runs. `tests/unit/hero-parity.test.tsx` checks the Hero against that markup.\n78\t- Content is inline JSX: copy lives in the components (e.g. `src/sections/Hero/Hero.tsx`). The typed `src/content/` layer described in `docs/architecture.md` does not exist yet.\n79\t\n80\t## Layers\n81\t\n82\t**App shell (`src/app/`):**\n83\t- Purpose: root composition and providers\n84\t- Location: `src/app/`\n85\t- Contains: `App.tsx`, `Providers.tsx`, `Page.tsx`\n86\t- Depends on: `src/anim` (via `Providers`), `src/sections`, `src/components/ui`\n87\t- Used by: `src/main.tsx`\n88\t\n89\t**Sections (`src/sections/`):**\n90\t- Purpose: page content blocks\n91\t- Location: `src/sections/<Name>/<Name>.tsx` (Hero) and `src/sections/Stubs/`\n92\t- Contains: section components taking no props today\n93\t- Depends on: `src/layout`, `src/anim` barrel (Hero imports `TextReveal`)\n94\t- Used by: `src/app/Page.tsx`\n95\t\n96\t**Layout (`src/layout/`):**\n97\t- Purpose: shared page structure\n98\t- Location: `src/layout/`\n99\t- Contains: `Section.tsx` (props: `id`, `title`, `className`, `children`), `Container.tsx`\n100\t- Depends on: `src/lib/utils.ts`\n101\t- Used by: sections\n102\t\n103\t**UI components (`src/components/ui/`):**\n104\t- Purpose: reusable interactive pieces\n105\t- Location: `src/components/ui/`\n106\t- Contains: `ThemeToggle.tsx` only. `Button`, `Tag`, `Card`, `Heading`, `Logo`, `Icon` are planned in `docs/architecture.md`.\n107\t- Depends on: `src/anim` barrel, `src/lib/theme.ts`, `src/lib/useTheme.ts`\n108\t- Used by: `src/app/App.tsx`, sections (planned)\n109\t\n110\t**Animation (`src/anim/`):**\n111\t- Purpose: the only layer that imports `motion/react` and `@react-spring/web`\n112\t- Location: `src/anim/`\n113\t- Contains: `index.ts` (barrel), `MotionPreferenceProvider.tsx`, `useMotionPreference.ts`, `tokens.ts`, `declarative/TextReveal.tsx`, `physics/ThemeThumb.tsx`\n114\t- Depends on: `motion/react`, `@react-spring/web`, `src/anim/tokens.ts`\n115\t- Used by: `src/app/Providers.tsx`, `src/components/ui/ThemeToggle.tsx`, `src/sections/Hero/Hero.tsx`\n116\t- Must not import: sections, layout, content (enforced by the `**/anim/**` override in `.oxlintrc.json`)\n117\t\n118\t**Lib and hooks (`src/lib/`):**\n119\t- Purpose: framework-agnostic helpers and the theme hook\n120\t- Location: `src/lib/theme.ts`, `src/lib/useTheme.ts`, `src/lib/utils.ts`\n121\t- Contains: theme read/apply/subscribe, `cn` class merge helper\n122\t- Used by: components. `src/lib/useTheme.ts` is the React hook for the theme value.\n123\t\n124\t**Styles (`src/styles/`):**\n125\t- Purpose: design tokens and global CSS\n126\t- Location: `src/styles/index.css` (entry, imported by `src/main.tsx`), `tokens.css`, `base.css`\n127\t- Contains: Tailwind v4 config in CSS (`@theme inline`, `@custom-variant dark`), `@source` directives for `index.html` and `src/`\n128\t\n129\t## Data Flow\n130\t\n131\t### Primary Request Path (page load)\n132\t\n133\t1. Browser loads `index.html`. The inline script in `<head>` reads `localStorage.theme`, falls back to `prefers-color-scheme`, and sets `data-theme` on `<html>` before first paint (`index.html`, lines 9-24).\n134\t2. Vite-built module `src/main.tsx` runs, imports `src/styles/index.css` and the Inter font, and calls `createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(...)` (`src/main.tsx`).\n135\t3. `App` renders `Providers` (which renders `MotionPreferenceProvider`), then the fixed `ThemeToggle` header, then `Page` (`src/app/App.tsx`, `src/app/Providers.tsx`).\n136\t4. `MotionPreferenceProvider` calls `useMotionPreference()`, sets react-spring `Globals.assign({ skipAnimation })`, and wraps children in `MotionConfig` (`src/anim/MotionPreferenceProvider.tsx`).\n137\t5. `Page` renders `<main id=\"main\">` with `Hero` and `SectionStubs` (`src/app/Page.tsx`).\n138\t\n139\t### Theme Toggle Path\n140\t\n141\t1. User clicks the button in `src/components/ui/ThemeToggle.tsx`. `toggle()` computes the next theme and calls `applyTheme(next)`.\n142\t2. `applyTheme` sets `html[data-theme]` first, so the switch always works, then writes `localStorage` in a try block (`src/lib/theme.ts`).\n143\t3. `useTheme` (`src/lib/useTheme.ts`) observes the attribute via `subscribeTheme`, so React re-renders the `aria-pressed` state.\n144\t4. `ThemeThumb` (`src/anim/physics/ThemeThumb.tsx`) animates the thumb with react-spring.\n145\t\n146\t### Cross-Tab and OS Theme Sync\n147\t\n148\t1. `subscribeTheme` in `src/lib/theme.ts` listens to `storage` events and to `prefers-color-scheme` `change` events.\n149\t2. When no stored choice exists, OS changes are followed. The attribute remains the single source of truth.\n150\t\n151\t### Motion Preference Path\n152\t\n153\t1. `useMotionPreference` (`src/anim/useMotionPreference.ts`) queries `(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`.\n154\t2. `MotionPreferenceProvider` maps that to `MotionConfig reducedMotion` (`'always'` or `'never'`) and to react-spring `skipAnimation`.\n155\t3. Base CSS applies reduced-motion guards (`src/styles/base.css`, `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`).\n156\t\n157\t**State Management:**\n158\t- No store library. Theme state lives in `html[data-theme]` plus `localStorage`. Motion preference is derived from `matchMedia`. Other UI state is local component state.\n159\t\n160\t## Key Abstractions\n161\t\n162\t**Animation barrel:**\n163\t- Purpose: one import path for all motion, so libraries can be swapped without touching sections\n164\t- Examples: `src/anim/index.ts`\n165\t- Pattern: re-export of semantic components and hooks. Current exports: `ThemeThumb`, `MotionPreferenceProvider`, `useMotionPreference`, `TextReveal`, `springs`, `durations`, `easeOut`.\n166\t- Usage: `import { TextReveal } from '@/anim'` (see `src/sections/Hero/Hero.tsx`)\n167\t\n168\t**Theme API:**\n169\t- Purpose: one module owns `data-theme` and storage\n170\t- Examples: `src/lib/theme.ts` exports `Theme`, `THEME_STORAGE_KEY`, `readTheme`, `applyTheme`, `subscribeTheme`\n171\t- Pattern: DOM attribute as state, React hook as a subscriber (`src/lib/useTheme.ts`)\n172\t\n173\t**Path alias:**\n174\t- `@/` maps to `src/` in `vite.config.ts`, `vitest.config.ts`, and `tsconfig.app.json` (`paths`)\n175\t- Use `@/sections/Hero/Hero`, not relative `../../` paths across layers\n176\t\n177\t## Entry Points\n178\t\n179\t**Browser entry:**\n180\t- Location: `index.html` (loads `/src/main.tsx` as a module script)\n181\t- Triggers: any page load of the deployed site or `npm run dev`\n182\t- Responsibilities: pre-paint theme script, static fallback markup, module bootstrap\n183\t\n184\t**React root:**\n185\t- Location: `src/main.tsx`\n186\t- Triggers: module evaluation\n187\t- Responsibilities: mount `<App />` into `#root`, global CSS import\n188\t\n189\t**Build entry:**\n190\t- Location: `vite.config.ts`\n191\t- Triggers: `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, `npm run preview`\n192\t- Responsibilities: base path from `VITE_BASE`, plugins (`react()`, `tailwindcss()`), `@` alias\n193\t\n194\t**Quality gate entry:**\n195\t- Location: `package.json` `verify` script, invoked by `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`\n196\t- Responsibilities: typecheck, lint, format, unit tests, source gates, build, dist gates\n197\t\n198\t## Architectural Constraints\n199\t\n200\t- **Threading:** Single-threaded browser main thread. No Web Workers in `src/`.\n201\t- **Global state:** `document.documentElement` `data-theme` attribute and `localStorage` key `theme` (`src/lib/theme.ts`). Module-level `Globals` from `@react-spring/web` is mutated by `src/anim/MotionPreferenceProvider.tsx`.\n202\t- **Circular imports:** None detected in the current `src/` tree.\n203\t- **Static output:** No server code. Anything served must exist in `public/` or be imported as a module so Vite hashes it.\n204\t- **Base path:** Absolute paths break under `VITE_BASE`. Use `import.meta.env.BASE_URL` (see `src/sections/Hero/Hero.tsx`) or `%BASE_URL%` in `index.html`.\n205\t- **Content rule:** A phone number must never appear in served output. `scripts/check-no-phone.mjs` enforces this over `dist/`.\n206\t\n207\t## Anti-Patterns\n208\t\n209\t### Hard-coded copy in index.html and components\n210\t\n211\t**What happens:** The Hero copy and the mailto link appear in both `src/sections/Hero/Hero.tsx` and the static markup in `index.html`.\n212\t**Why it's wrong:** Edits to one copy drift from the other. `tests/unit/hero-parity.test.tsx` only catches drift in what it checks.\n213\t**Do this instead:** Change the component and the pre-rendered markup together, and keep `tests/unit/hero-parity.test.tsx` passing.\n214\t\n215\t### Importing animation libraries outside src/anim\n216\t\n217\t**What happens:** Nothing in `src/` does this today. The pattern to avoid is `import { motion } from 'motion/react'` inside `src/sections/` or `src/layout/`.\n218\t**Why it's wrong:** `oxlint` fails the build (`no-restricted-imports` in `.oxlintrc.json`), and the animation barrel is then bypassed.\n219\t**Do this instead:** Add a semantic wrapper in `src/anim/declarative/` or `src/anim/physics/`, export it from `src/anim/index.ts`, then import from `@/anim`.\n220\t\n221\t### Writing theme state without applyTheme\n222\t\n223\t**What happens:** Setting `data-theme` directly, or calling `localStorage.setItem('theme', ...)` from a component.\n224\t**Why it's wrong:** The attribute and the stored value drift, and `subscribeTheme` treats the attribute as the source of truth.\n225\t**Do this instead:** Call `applyTheme(next)` from `src/lib/theme.ts`.\n226\t\n227\t## Error Handling\n228\t\n229\t**Strategy:** Defensive fallbacks, no thrown errors in the app path.\n230\t\n231\t**Patterns:**\n232\t- `localStorage` access is wrapped in try/catch (`src/lib/theme.ts` `applyTheme`, `storedTheme`; `index.html` inline script). Blocked storage falls back to in-memory choice.\n233\t- `window.matchMedia` access is wrapped in try/catch with a `light` fallback (`src/lib/theme.ts` `systemTheme`, `subscribeTheme`).\n234\t- `document.getElementById('root')!` in `src/main.tsx` assumes the root exists; there is no runtime guard.\n235\t\n236\t## Cross-Cutting Concerns\n237\t\n238\t**Logging:** None in app code. Build scripts print to stdout or stderr (`scripts/check-no-phone.mjs`).\n239\t**Validation:** Typecheck via `tsc -b` with `strict`, `noUnusedLocals`, `noUnusedParameters` (`tsconfig.app.json`). Runtime validation of theme values uses `isTheme` (`src/lib/theme.ts`).\n240\t**Authentication:** Not applicable. No user accounts.\n241\t**Accessibility:** Each section is a `<section>` labelled by its heading via `aria-labelledby` (`src/layout/Section.tsx`). The theme toggle exposes `aria-pressed` and `aria-label` (`src/components/ui/ThemeToggle.tsx`).\n242\t\n243\t## Planned but Not Yet Present\n244\t\n245\tThese are described in `docs/architecture.md` and do not exist in the repo as of this analysis. Plan against the tracked files, and verify before depending on them:\n246\t- `src/content/` (typed content schema and per-section data modules). Copy currently lives in components.\n247\t- `src/hooks/` (`useActiveSection`, `useMediaQuery`, `useHoverCapable`). The only hook present is `src/lib/useTheme.ts`.\n248\t- `src/components/motion-primitives/` (vendored primitives). `tests/fixtures/motion-primitives/Ok.tsx` exists as a test input.\n249\t- `src/assets/images/` and vite-imagetools image pipeline.\n250\t- Section components beyond Hero (About, Experience, Projects, Skills, Education, Contact). They exist only as stubs.\n251\t- Lenis smooth scroll, lucide-react icons.\n252\t\n253\t---\n254\t\n255\t*Architecture analysis: Two React contexts exist (motion preference and, via the DOM, theme).\n\n**Key Characteristics:**\n- Static output only: `npm run build` produces `dist/`; no runtime server or API calls.\n- The DOM is the source of truth for theme: `html[data-theme]` is read by `readTheme()` and written by `applyTheme()` and the pre-paint script in `index.html`.\n- Animation is isolated behind one barrel (`src/anim/index.ts`). When no stored choice exists, OS changes are followed. The attribute remains the single source of truth.\n\n### Motion Preference Path\n\n1. `useMotionPreference` (`src/anim/useMotionPreference.ts`) queries `(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`.\n2. `MotionPreferenceProvider` maps that to `MotionConfig reducedMotion` (`'always'` or `'never'`) and to react-spring `skipAnimation`.\n3. Theme state lives in `html[data-theme]` plus `localStorage`. Motion preference is derived from `matchMedia`. Other UI state is local component state.\n\n## Key Abstractions\n\n**Animation barrel:**\n- Purpose: one import path for all motion, so libraries can be swapped without touching sections\n- Examples: `src/anim/index.ts`\n- Pattern: re-export of semantic components and hooks. Current exports: `ThemeThumb`, `MotionPreferenceProvider`, `useMotionPreference`, `TextReveal`, `springs`, `durations`, `easeOut`.\n- Usage: `import { TextReveal } from '@/anim'` (see `src/sections/Hero/Hero.tsx`)\n\n**Theme API:**\n- Purpose: one module owns `data-theme` and storage\n- Examples: `src/lib/theme.ts` exports `Theme`, `THEME_STORAGE_KEY`, `readTheme`, `applyTheme`, `subscribeTheme`\n- Pattern: DOM attribute as state, React hook as a subscriber (`src/lib/useTheme.ts`)\n\n**Path alias:**\n- `@/` maps to `src/` in `vite.config.ts`, `vitest.config.ts`, and `tsconfig.app.json` (`paths`)\n- Use `@/sections/Hero/Hero`, not relative `../../` paths across layers\n\n## Entry Points\n\n**Browser entry:**\n- Location: `index.html` (loads `/src/main.tsx` as a module script)\n- Triggers: any page load of the deployed site or `npm run dev`\n- Responsibilities: pre-paint theme script, static fallback markup, module bootstrap\n\n**React root:**\n- Location: `src/main.tsx`\n- Triggers: module evaluation\n- Responsibilities: mount `<App />` into `#root`, global CSS import\n\n**Build entry:**\n- Location: `vite.config.ts`\n- Triggers: `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, `npm run preview`\n- Responsibilities: base path from `VITE_BASE`, plugins (`react()`, `tailwindcss()`), `@` alias\n\n**Quality gate entry:**\n- Location: `package.json` `verify` script, invoked by `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`\n- Responsibilities: typecheck, lint, format, unit tests, source gates, build, dist gates\n\n## Architectural Constraints\n\n- **Threading:** Single-threaded browser main thread. No Web Workers in `src/`.\n- **Global state:** `document.documentElement` `data-theme` attribute and `localStorage` key `theme` (`src/lib/theme.ts`). Module-level `Globals` from `@react-spring/web` is mutated by `src/anim/MotionPreferenceProvider.tsx`.\n- **Circular imports:** None detected in the current `src/` tree.\n- **Static output:** No server code. Anything served must exist in `public/` or be imported as a module so Vite hashes it.\n- **Base path:** Absolute paths break under `VITE_BASE`. Use `import.meta.env.BASE_URL` (see `src/sections/Hero/Hero.tsx`) or `%BASE_URL%` in `index.html`.\n- **Content rule:** A phone number must never appear in served output. `scripts/check-no-phone.mjs` enforces this over `dist/`.\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n### Hard-coded copy in index.html and components\n\n**What happens:** The Hero copy and the mailto link appear in both `src/sections/Hero/Hero.tsx` and the static markup in `index.html`.\n**Why it's wrong:** Edits to one copy drift from the other. `tests/unit/hero-parity.test.tsx` only catches drift in what it checks.\n**Do this instead:** Change the component and the pre-rendered markup together, and keep `tests/unit/hero-parity.test.tsx` passing.\n\n### Importing animation libraries outside src/anim\n\n**What happens:** Nothing in `src/` does this today. The pattern to avoid is `import { motion } from 'motion/react'` inside `src/sections/` or `src/layout/`.\n**Why it's wrong:** `oxlint` fails the build (`no-restricted-imports` in `.oxlintrc.json`), and the animation barrel is then bypassed.\n**Do this instead:** Add a semantic wrapper in `src/anim/declarative/` or `src/anim/physics/`, export it from `src/anim/index.ts`, then import from `@/anim`.\n\n### Writing theme state without applyTheme\n\n**What happens:** Setting `data-theme` directly, or calling `localStorage.setItem('theme', ...)` from a component.\n**Why it's wrong:** The attribute and the stored value drift, and `subscribeTheme` treats the attribute as the source of truth.\n**Do this instead:** Call `applyTheme(next)` from `src/lib/theme.ts`.\n\n## Error Handling\n\n**Strategy:** Defensive fallbacks, no thrown errors in the app path.\n\n**Patterns:**\n- `localStorage` access is wrapped in try/catch (`src/lib/theme.ts` `applyTheme`, `storedTheme`; `index.html` inline script). Blocked storage falls back to in-memory choice.\n- `window.matchMedia` access is wrapped in try/catch with a `light` fallback (`src/lib/theme.ts` `systemTheme`, `subscribeTheme`).\n- `document.getElementById('root')!` in `src/main.tsx` assumes the root exists; there is no runtime guard.\n\n## Cross-Cutting Concerns\n\n**Logging:** None in app code. Build scripts print to stdout or stderr (`scripts/check-no-phone.mjs`).\n**Validation:** Typecheck via `tsc -b` with `strict`, `noUnusedLocals`, `noUnusedParameters` (`tsconfig.app.json`). Runtime validation of theme values uses `isTheme` (`src/lib/theme.ts`).\n**Authentication:** Not applicable. No user accounts.\n**Accessibility:** Each section is a `<section>` labelled by its heading via `aria-labelledby` (`src/layout/Section.tsx`). The theme toggle exposes `aria-pressed` and `aria-label` (`src/components/ui/ThemeToggle.tsx`).\n\n## Planned but Not Yet Present\n\nThese are described in `docs/architecture.md` and do not exist in the repo as of this analysis. Plan against the tracked files, and verify before depending on them:\n- `src/content/` (typed content schema and per-section data modules). Copy currently lives in components.\n- `src/hooks/` (`useActiveSection`, `useMediaQuery`, `useHoverCapable`). The only hook present is `src/lib/useTheme.ts`.\n- `src/components/motion-primitives/` (vendored primitives). `tests/fixtures/motion-primitives/Ok.tsx` exists as a test input.\n- `src/assets/images/` and vite-imagetools image pipeline.\n- Section components beyond Hero (About, Experience, Projects, Skills, Education, Contact). Hooks: camelCase with `use` prefix in `.ts`, e.g. `src/lib/useTheme.ts`, `src/anim/useMotionPreference.ts`\n- Non-component modules: camelCase `.ts`, e.g. `src/lib/theme.ts`, `src/anim/tokens.ts`\n- `tests/e2e/`\n- Docs: UPPERCASE for planning docs (`PROJECT.md`), `docs/architecture.md` lowercase, ADRs as `NNNN-kebab-title.md`\n\n**Directories:**\n- Lowercase: `src/lib/`, `src/anim/`, `src/styles/`\n- Feature folders for sections use PascalCase: `src/sections/Hero/`, `src/sections/Stubs/`\n- Sub-role folders inside `anim/` use lowercase: `declarative/`, `physics/`\n\n**Exports:**\n- Section and component modules use named exports (`export function Hero()`), not default exports. Exception: `vite.config.ts`, `vitest.config.ts`, `playwright.config.ts` use default exports as config requires.\n- Shared helpers are named exports from `src/lib/` and `src/anim/tokens.ts`.\n\n**Imports:**\n- Use the `@/` alias for anything under `src/` (for example `import { TextReveal } from '@/anim'`). Relative imports are used only within a folder.\n\n## Where to Add New Code\n\n**New Section (e.g. About, Projects):**\n- Implementation: `src/sections/<Name>/<Name>.tsx` (named export, props typed inline)\n- Replace the matching stub in `src/sections/Stubs/SectionStubs.tsx`, and add the component to `src/app/Page.tsx` in the desired order\n- Use `Section` from `src/layout/Section.tsx` for the outer `<section>` and heading\n- Matching static markup for `index.html`: keep in step with the component (see `ARCHITECTURE.md`, Anti-Patterns)\n- Tests: `tests/unit/<name>.test.tsx`\n\n**New Reusable UI Component:**\n- Implementation: `src/components/ui/<Name>.tsx`\n- Tests: `tests/unit/<name>.test.tsx`\n\n**New Layout Primitive:**\n- Implementation: `src/layout/<Name>.tsx`\n\n**New Animation Wrapper:**\n- Motion-owned: `src/anim/declarative/<Name>.tsx`\n- react-spring-owned: `src/anim/physics/<Name>.tsx`\n- Export from `src/anim/index.ts`. <action>\n123\tAll four files live in the phase directory per D-01; wireframes are ASCII/markdown per D-02. This task builds one section through every planning-doc layer; other sections are added by plans 01-03, 01-04, 01-05 and 01-07 into the same files.\n124\t\n125\t(1) contrast-check.mjs — a Node ESM script using only node: built-ins (fs, path, process). No package.json, no npm install. It is a verification tool for the tokens doc, not application code (Phase 2 may port its logic into a token-contrast test). Implement: hex parsing; OKLCH to OKLab to linear sRGB using Ottosson's published matrices; a gamut check (each linear channel within -0.0001..1.0001, otherwise the row FAILs as OUT-OF-GAMUT, because browser gamut mapping would change the rendered color); WCAG 2.x relative luminance (0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B on linear channels); contrast (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05), compared UNROUNDED against the threshold (4.499 fails 4.5) and printed to 2 decimals. Implement CSS color-mix(in oklch) semantics for derived tokens: mix(--a P%, --b) interpolates L and C linearly with weight P/100 on --a, hue along the shorter arc, and an achromatic color (C below 0.0001) adopts the other color's hue. Argument flags may appear before or after the doc path. Modes:\n126\t- --selftest: runs at least 9 checks and prints SELFTEST PASS n/n with exit 0, or one SELFTEST FAIL line per failed check with exit 1. Required checks: hex pairs 050315/fbfbfe = 19.73, 2f27ce/fbfbfe = 8.83, 2f27ce/050315 = 2.23, 433bff/050315 = 3.21, 7b75ff/050315 = 5.66, dedcff/fbfbfe = 1.29 (each within 0.01; values independently verified during planning); oklch(1 0 0) vs oklch(0 0 0) = 21.00; hex 2f27ce round-trips through OKLCH back to 2f27ce; a 50% mix of oklch(1 0 0) and oklch(0 0 0) has L = 0.5.\n127\t- --convert VALUE: given a hex prints oklch(L C H) (L as 0-1 decimal, 4 decimals), given oklch(...) prints hex. Used to author tokens and realtimecolors links.\n128\t- default, DOC [--require-chosen]: parse fenced blocks from DOC. Info string \"palette X\" (X = one uppercase letter) holds role lines \"THEME TOKEN oklch(L C H)\" (THEME is light or dark) and optional derived-override lines. Info string \"derived\" holds lines \"THEME TOKEN mix(TOKEN_A P%, TOKEN_B)\". Info string \"pairs\" holds lines \"FG on BG CATEGORY USED-BY...\" where CATEGORY is text (min 4.5), large (3.0), ui (3.0) or focus (3.0). Enforce per D-06: every palette defines exactly the 5 roles --text, --background, --primary, --secondary, --accent for both light and dark; a derived token given a literal color is an error (derived tokens are mix() only); every pair token resolves. First print one line per resolved token, \"TOKEN PALETTE THEME NAME oklch(L C H) #rrggbb\" (roles and derived tokens alike), then print one row per palette x theme x pair: \"PALETTE THEME FG on BG CATEGORY RATIO min THRESHOLD PASS|FAIL USED-BY\". Final line: \"RESULT: PASS palettes=N checks=M\" with exit 0, or \"RESULT: FAIL failures=K\" with exit 1. Exit 2 with an \"ERROR:\" line when no palette block or no pairs line is found, or any block fails to parse. With --require-chosen the doc must contain a line \"Chosen palette: X\" naming an existing palette block (print \"CHOSEN X\"), else exit 1.\n129\t\n130\t(2) 01-DESIGN-TOKENS.md — first line after the title: \"Status: Draft\". This task builds one section through every planning-doc layer; other sections are added by plans 01-03, 01-04, 01-05 and 01-07 into the same files.\n\n(1) contrast-check.mjs — a Node ESM script using only node: built-ins (fs, path, process). No package.json, no npm install. It is a verification tool for the tokens doc, not application code (Phase 2 may port its logic into a token-contrast test). Implement: hex parsing; OKLCH to OKLab to linear sRGB using Ottosson's published matrices; a gamut check (each linear channel within -0.0001..1.0001, otherwise the row FAILs as OUT-OF-GAMUT, because browser gamut mapping would change the rendered color); WCAG 2.x relative luminance (0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B on linear channels); contrast (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05), compared UNROUNDED against the threshold (4.499 fails 4.5) and printed to 2 decimals. Implement CSS color-mix(in oklch) semantics for derived tokens: mix(--a P%, --b) interpolates L and C linearly with weight P/100 on --a, hue along the shorter arc, and an achromatic color (C below 0.0001) adopts the other color's hue. Argument flags may appear before or after the doc path. Modes:\n- --selftest: runs at least 9 checks and prints SELFTEST PASS n/n with exit 0, or one SELFTEST FAIL line per failed check with exit 1. Required checks: hex pairs 050315/fbfbfe = 19.73, 2f27ce/fbfbfe = 8.83, 2f27ce/050315 = 2.23, 433bff/050315 = 3.21, 7b75ff/050315 = 5.66, dedcff/fbfbfe = 1.29 (each within 0.01; values independently verified during planning); oklch(1 0 0) vs oklch(0 0 0) = 21.00; hex 2f27ce round-trips through OKLCH back to 2f27ce; a 50% mix of oklch(1 0 0) and oklch(0 0 0) has L = 0.5.\n- --convert VALUE: given a hex prints oklch(L C H) (L as 0-1 decimal, 4 decimals), given oklch(...) prints hex. Used to author tokens and realtimecolors links.\n- default, DOC [--require-chosen]: parse fenced blocks from DOC. Info string \"palette X\" (X = one uppercase letter) holds role lines \"THEME TOKEN oklch(L C H)\" (THEME is light or dark) and optional derived-override lines. Info string \"derived\" holds lines \"THEME TOKEN mix(TOKEN_A P%, TOKEN_B)\". Info string \"pairs\" holds lines \"FG on BG CATEGORY USED-BY...\" where CATEGORY is text (min 4.5), large (3.0), ui (3.0) or focus (3.0). Enforce per D-06: every palette defines exactly the 5 roles --text, --background, --primary, --secondary, --accent for both light and dark; a derived token given a literal color is an error (derived tokens are mix() only); every pair token resolves. First print one line per resolved token, \"TOKEN PALETTE THEME NAME oklch(L C H) #rrggbb\" (roles and derived tokens alike), then print one row per palette x theme x pair: \"PALETTE THEME FG on BG CATEGORY RATIO min THRESHOLD PASS|FAIL USED-BY\". Final line: \"RESULT: PASS palettes=N checks=M\" with exit 0, or \"RESULT: FAIL failures=K\" with exit 1. Exit 2 with an \"ERROR:\" line when no palette block or no pairs line is found, or any block fails to parse. With --require-chosen the doc must contain a line \"Chosen palette: X\" naming an existing palette block (print \"CHOSEN X\"), else exit 1.\n\n(2) 01-DESIGN-TOKENS.md — first line after the title: \"Status: Draft\". One format is used for every date on the site and in this file.\n\n1. Month names are written in full: January, February, and so on. No abbreviations, no numeric months.\n2. A single date is `Month YYYY`, for example `July 2026`.\n3. A range is `Month YYYY – Month YYYY`: an en dash (U+2013) with one space on each side, and the year written on both sides, for example `May 2025 – August 2025`.\n4. Resume abbreviations are expanded. The resume's `Aug. 2022` becomes `August 2022`.\n5. Legacy hyphen ranges and short months are normalized. The legacy `June 2023 - Aug 2023` becomes `June 2023 – August 2023`.\n6. Academic-term labels (Spring 2024, Fall 2023, Summer 2022) are converted to month ranges per the G-08 ruling. The original label is kept in the item's Legacy-site value.\n7. This policy is applied to every date in the file. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01FuRuUZoec59NYu4RbgLxwj","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Design Tokens (DOC-04)\n2\t\n3\tStatus: Accepted\n4\t\n5\tChosen palette: A\n6\t\n7\tPhase 1 plan 01-01 created this file with candidate A and the Contact Me slice of the contrast matrix. Plan 01-04 added candidates B and C, the full 19-pair list for every section, the type pairing per candidate, and, after the user picked candidate A (tuned seed indigo, Inter only), the chosen system below.\n8\t\n9\tOwner decisions this file records: D-04 (three candidates, per-theme tokens, the user picks one), D-05 (type explored with color), D-06 (exactly 5 role tokens plus derived tints). WCAG 2.2 AA is the bar.\n10\t\n11\t## Format\n12\t\n13\tTokens live in fenced blocks so a script can recompute every contrast ratio from the OKLCH values instead of trusting the author. There are three block types, identified by the fence info string:\n14\t\n15\t- `palette X` (X is one capital letter) holds one palette. Each line is a theme, a token name and an OKLCH color, for example `light --text oklch(L C H)`, where L is lightness from 0 to 1, C is chroma and H is hue in degrees. THEME is `light` or `dark`. Every palette must define exactly the five role tokens for both themes (10 lines). A palette block may also carry derived-override lines (a `mix()` formula) when one palette needs a different derived formula than the shared one.\n16\t- `derived` holds tints computed from the roles. Each line is a theme, a token name and `mix(--a P%, --b)`, which matches CSS `color-mix(in oklch, var(--a) P%, var(--b))`: lightness and chroma blend linearly, hue goes along the shorter arc, and an achromatic color takes the other color's hue. A derived token may never be given a literal color. That is what makes a palette swap a single-block edit (D-06): only the five role lines change, and every derived token follows.\n17\t- `pairs` holds the contrast matrix. Each line is `FG on BG CATEGORY USED-BY`, where CATEGORY is `text` (needs 4.5:1), `large` (3:1), `ui` (3:1) or `focus` (3:1), and USED-BY names the section anchor and the element. Every pair is evaluated for every palette in both themes.\n18\t\n19\tA final line `Chosen palette: X` (written once the user picks) names the palette that ships. It is written as plain text on its own line, outside any fence.\n20\t\n21\tVerify with `node contrast-check.mjs 01-DESIGN-TOKENS.md` from this directory. The last line is `RESULT: PASS palettes=N checks=M` and the exit code is 0 only when every pair passes. Add `--require-chosen` once the choice is made. `--convert VALUE` turns a hex into OKLCH (rounded to stay inside the sRGB gamut) or an OKLCH into a hex, and is how role values and realtimecolors links are authored. `--selftest` proves the checker against independently computed ratios.\n22\t\n23\tRatios are compared unrounded against the threshold (4.499 fails 4.5) and printed to two decimals. A color outside the sRGB gamut fails its rows as OUT-OF-GAMUT, because the browser would remap it and the ratio would no longer be the one that was checked.\n24\t\n25\t## Role tokens\n26\t\n27\tThe five roles follow the realtimecolors order. Per-theme values are mandatory (D-04): the seed indigo `2f27ce` measures 2.23:1 on the dark background `050315`, which fails text, UI and focus use.\n28\t\n29\t| Order | Token | Job |\n30\t|-------|-------|-----|\n31\t| 1 | `--text` | Body and heading text, and the on-color for filled dark surfaces |\n32\t| 2 | `--background` | Page background |\n33\t| 3 | `--primary` | Filled buttons, the main brand fill |\n34\t| 4 | `--secondary` | Tint family for cards and soft fills (decorative, never text or a border on its own: `dedcff` on the light background is 1.29:1) |\n35\t| 5 | `--accent` | Highlights and large display color |\n36\t\n37\tDerived tokens (D-06), all `mix()` of roles, defined once for every candidate in the shared `derived` block:\n38\t\n39\t| Token | Job |\n40\t|-------|-----|\n41\t| `--surface` | Card, toast and overlay panel fill |\n42\t| `--muted` | Dates, captions and secondary copy |\n43\t| `--border` | Decorative hairlines (no contrast requirement) |\n44\t| `--border-strong` | Control boundaries (3:1) |\n45\t| `--link` | Inline link text |\n46\t| `--on-primary` | Label on a filled primary button |\n47\t| `--on-accent` | Label on an accent chip or active pill |\n48\t| `--primary-hover` | Hovered or pressed filled button |\n49\t| `--focus-ring` | Keyboard focus indicator |\n50\t\n51\t## Candidate A — Tuned seed indigo\n52\t\n53\tChosen.\n54\t\n55\tContinuity with the realtimecolors seed (050315 / fbfbfe / 2f27ce / dedcff / 433bff). Dark roles are authored for dark, not inverted: the text and background swap ends, primary and accent lift to the 5.66:1 and 8.19:1 class on `050315`, and secondary becomes a dark indigo tint. One tune from the seed in light: `--primary` moves from `2f27ce` to `5046e5` (plan 01-01 had first tuned it to `281fb4`; the full 19-pair set forces a second move). Reason: a focus ring must hold 3:1 against the page, a card, the secondary tint and a filled primary button. With `281fb4` no ring color does all four: a mid-tone ring clears the button but gives 2.50:1 on the secondary tint, and a near-black ring gives 1.89:1 on the button. A primary lighter than the seed's (relative luminance about 0.11 to 0.18) opens the band: a near-black ring then reads on the button (3.2:1 or better) and on every light surface, while the white label on the button still holds 4.5:1. Cost: primary `5046e5` and accent `433bff` are now close in light, so color alone never separates them (Pitfall 5); state uses shape and weight too.\n56\t\n57\tType pairing: Inter variable for display and body, one family: `@fontsource-variable/inter` 5.3.0. This is the seed pairing from realtimecolors and the safest for mobile weight (one latin subset, 48 kB).\n58\t\n59\tSwatches (hex of the OKLCH roles below, for reference):\n60\t\n61\t| Role | Light | Dark |\n62\t|------|-------|------|\n63\t| --text | #050315 | #fbfbfe |\n64\t| --background | #fbfbfe | #050315 |\n65\t| --primary | #5046e5 | #7b75ff |\n66\t| --secondary | #dedcff | #1c1950 |\n67\t| --accent | #433bff | #9d99ff |\n68\t\n69\t```palette A\n70\tlight --text oklch(0.1190 0.0436 285.36)\n71\tlight --background oklch(0.9889 0.0039 286.33)\n72\tlight --primary oklch(0.5113 0.2298 277.28)\n73\tlight --secondary oklch(0.9070 0.0475 288.03)\n74\tlight --accent oklch(0.5143 0.2729 272.97)\n75\tdark --text oklch(0.9889 0.0039 286.33)\n76\tdark --background oklch(0.1190 0.0436 285.36)\n77\tdark --primary oklch(0.6383 0.1988 281.11)\n78\tdark --secondary oklch(0.2561 0.0973 279.44)\n79\tdark --accent oklch(0.7288 0.1457 283.95)\n80\t```\n81\t\n82\tPreview:\n83\t\n84\t- Light: https://www.realtimecolors.com/?colors=050315-fbfbfe-5046e5-dedcff-433bff&fonts=Inter-Inter\n85\t- Dark: https://www.realtimecolors.com/?colors=fbfbfe-050315-7b75ff-1c1950-9d99ff&fonts=Inter-Inter\n86\t\n87\tRationale: Personality: Crafted, Confident, Fast and Inclusive lead. Plan 01-04 added candidates B and C, the full 19-pair list for every section, the type pairing per candidate, and, after the user picked candidate A (tuned seed indigo, Inter only), the chosen system below.\n\nOwner decisions this file records: D-04 (three candidates, per-theme tokens, the user picks one), D-05 (type explored with color), D-06 (exactly 5 role tokens plus derived tints). WCAG 2.2 AA is the bar.\n\n## Format\n\nTokens live in fenced blocks so a script can recompute every contrast ratio from the OKLCH values instead of trusting the author. There are three block types, identified by the fence info string:\n\n- `palette X` (X is one capital letter) holds one palette. Each line is a theme, a token name and an OKLCH color, for example `light --text oklch(L C H)`, where L is lightness from 0 to 1, C is chroma and H is hue in degrees. THEME is `light` or `dark`. Every palette must define exactly the five role tokens for both themes (10 lines). A palette block may also carry derived-override lines (a `mix()` formula) when one palette needs a different derived formula than the shared one.\n- `derived` holds tints computed from the roles. Each line is a theme, a token name and `mix(--a P%, --b)`, which matches CSS `color-mix(in oklch, var(--a) P%, var(--b))`: lightness and chroma blend linearly, hue goes along the shorter arc, and an achromatic color takes the other color's hue. A derived token may never be given a literal color. That is what makes a palette swap a single-block edit (D-06): only the five role lines change, and every derived token follows.\n- `pairs` holds the contrast matrix. Each line is `FG on BG CATEGORY USED-BY`, where CATEGORY is `text` (needs 4.5:1), `large` (3:1), `ui` (3:1) or `focus` (3:1), and USED-BY names the section anchor and the element. Every pair is evaluated for every palette in both themes.\n\nA final line `Chosen palette: X` (written once the user picks) names the palette that ships. It is written as plain text on its own line, outside any fence.\n\nVerify with `node contrast-check.mjs 01-DESIGN-TOKENS.md` from this directory. The last line is `RESULT: PASS palettes=N checks=M` and the exit code is 0 only when every pair passes. Add `--require-chosen` once the choice is made. `--convert VALUE` turns a hex into OKLCH (rounded to stay inside the sRGB gamut) or an OKLCH into a hex, and is how role values and realtimecolors links are authored. `--selftest` proves the checker against independently computed ratios.\n\nRatios are compared unrounded against the threshold (4.499 fails 4.5) and printed to two decimals. A color outside the sRGB gamut fails its rows as OUT-OF-GAMUT, because the browser would remap it and the ratio would no longer be the one that was checked.\n\n## Role tokens\n\nThe five roles follow the realtimecolors order. Per-theme values are mandatory (D-04): the seed indigo `2f27ce` measures 2.23:1 on the dark background `050315`, which fails text, UI and focus use.\n\n| Order | Token | Job |\n|-------|-------|-----|\n| 1 | `--text` | Body and heading text, and the on-color for filled dark surfaces |\n| 2 | `--background` | Page background |\n| 3 | `--primary` | Filled buttons, the main brand fill |\n| 4 | `--secondary` | Tint family for cards and soft fills (decorative, never text or a border on its own: `dedcff` on the light background is 1.29:1) |\n| 5 | `--accent` | Highlights and large display color |\n\nDerived tokens (D-06), all `mix()` of roles, defined once for every candidate in the shared `derived` block:\n\n| Token | Job |\n|-------|-----|\n| `--surface` | Card, toast and overlay panel fill |\n| `--muted` | Dates, captions and secondary copy |\n| `--border` | Decorative hairlines (no contrast requirement) |\n| `--border-strong` | Control boundaries (3:1) |\n| `--link` | Inline link text |\n| `--on-primary` | Label on a filled primary button |\n| `--on-accent` | Label on an accent chip or active pill |\n| `--primary-hover` | Hovered or pressed filled button |\n| `--focus-ring` | Keyboard focus indicator |\n\n## Candidate A — Tuned seed indigo\n\nChosen.\n\nContinuity with the realtimecolors seed (050315 / fbfbfe / 2f27ce / dedcff / 433bff). Dark roles are authored for dark, not inverted: the text and background swap ends, primary and accent lift to the 5.66:1 and 8.19:1 class on `050315`, and secondary becomes a dark indigo tint. One tune from the seed in light: `--primary` moves from `2f27ce` to `5046e5` (plan 01-01 had first tuned it to `281fb4`; the full 19-pair set forces a second move). Reason: a focus ring must hold 3:1 against the page, a card, the secondary tint and a filled primary button. With `281fb4` no ring color does all four: a mid-tone ring clears the button but gives 2.50:1 on the secondary tint, and a near-black ring gives 1.89:1 on the button. A primary lighter than the seed's (relative luminance about 0.11 to 0.18) opens the band: a near-black ring then reads on the button (3.2:1 or better) and on every light surface, while the white label on the button still holds 4.5:1. Cost: primary `5046e5` and accent `433bff` are now close in light, so color alone never separates them (Pitfall 5); state uses shape and weight too.\n\nType pairing: Inter variable for display and body, one family: `@fontsource-variable/inter` 5.3.0. This is the seed pairing from realtimecolors and the safest for mobile weight (one latin subset, 48 kB).\n\nSwatches (hex of the OKLCH roles below, for reference):\n\n| Role | Light | Dark |\n|------|-------|------|\n| --text | #050315 | #fbfbfe |\n| --background | #fbfbfe | #050315 |\n| --primary | #5046e5 | #7b75ff |\n| --secondary | #dedcff | #1c1950 |\n| --accent | #433bff | #9d99ff |\n\n```palette A\nlight --text oklch(0.1190 0.0436 285.36)\nlight --background oklch(0.9889 0.0039 286.33)\nlight --primary oklch(0.5113 0.2298 277.28)\nlight --secondary oklch(0.9070 0.0475 288.03)\nlight --accent oklch(0.5143 0.2729 272.97)\ndark --text oklch(0.9889 0.0039 286.33)\ndark --background oklch(0.1190 0.0436 285.36)\ndark --primary oklch(0.6383 0.1988 281.11)\ndark --secondary oklch(0.2561 0.0973 279.44)\ndark --accent oklch(0.7288 0.1457 283.95)\n```\n\nPreview:\n\n- Light: https://www.realtimecolors.com/?colors=050315-fbfbfe-5046e5-dedcff-433bff&fonts=Inter-Inter\n- Dark: https://www.realtimecolors.com/?colors=fbfbfe-050315-7b75ff-1c1950-9d99ff&fonts=Inter-Inter\n\nRationale: Personality: Crafted, Confident, Fast and Inclusive lead. A single family, a cool indigo on near-white and a near-black ink read as precise and quick; the focus ring and contrast are the most conservative of the three. It is the least Warm and least Playful of the set: the warmth and play would have to come from motion and shape alone, and indigo on near-white is the most common portfolio look. Pick A if continuity with the linked seed matters more than a distinct identity.\n\nContrast results:\n\n| Pair | Category | Light | Dark |\n|------|----------|-------|------|\n| --text on --background | text | 19.73 | 19.73 |\n| --text on --surface | text | 18.36 | 17.75 |\n| --text on --secondary | text | 15.32 | 15.59 |\n| --muted on --background | text | 9.79 | 8.96 |\n| --muted on --surface | text | 9.11 | 8.06 |\n| --link on --background | text | 8.35 | 8.19 |\n| --link on --surface | text | 7.77 | 7.36 |\n| --on-primary on --primary | text | 6.07 | 5.66 |\n| --on-primary on --primary-hover | text | 7.74 | 5.01 |\n| --on-accent on --accent | text | 6.15 | 8.19 |\n| --border-strong on --background | ui | 5.61 | 5.10 |\n| --border-strong on --surface | ui | 5.22 | 4.58 |\n| --primary on --background | ui | 6.07 | 5.66 |\n| --accent on --background | ui | 6.15 | 8.19 |\n| --accent on --surface | ui | 5.72 | 7.36 |\n| --focus-ring on --background | focus | 19.73 | 19.73 |\n| --focus-ring on --surface | focus | 18.36 | 17.75 |\n| --focus-ring on --primary | focus | 3.25 | 3.49 |\n| --focus-ring on --secondary | focus | 15.32 | 15.59 |\n\n## Shared derived tokens\n\nNine derived tokens, defined once and shared by A, B and C. Each is a `mix()` of roles (D-06), so a palette swap edits only the ten role lines. `--link` in dark is the lifted accent for candidate A (blending the dark primary toward near-white leaves the sRGB gamut and the checker reports OUT-OF-GAMUT); B and C override it inside their palette blocks. `--on-primary` and `--on-accent` are the page background in both themes (a light label on the deep light fills, a dark label on the lifted dark fills). `--primary-hover` is the primary pulled slightly toward the text color in light and toward the background in dark (mixing a lifted dark primary toward near-white leaves the gamut), so the button always reads as pressed in. `--focus-ring` is the text color in both themes: it is the only color that holds 3:1 against the page, a card, the secondary tint and a filled primary at once, once the light primary sits in the band described under candidate A.\n\n```derived\nlight --surface mix(--secondary 30%, --background)\ndark --surface mix(--secondary 60%, --background)\nlight --muted mix(--text 70%, --background)\ndark --muted mix(--text 72%, --background)\nlight --border mix(--text 14%, --background)\ndark --border mix(--text 16%, --background)\nlight --border-strong mix(--text 55%, --background)\ndark --border-strong mix(--text 55%, --background)\nlight --link mix(--primary 80%, --text)\ndark --link mix(--accent 100%, --background)\nlight --on-primary mix(--background 100%, --text)\ndark --on-primary mix(--background 100%, --text)\nlight --on-accent mix(--background 100%, --text)\ndark --on-accent mix(--background 100%, --text)\nlight --primary-hover mix(--primary 85%, --text)\ndark --primary-hover mix(--primary 94%, --background)\nlight --focus-ring mix(--text 100%, --background)\ndark --focus-ring mix(--text 100%, --background)\n```\n\n## Candidate B — Clay and cream\n\nNot chosen.\n\nWarm clay on cream. It carries no contrast requirement and is never the only cue for a control boundary; controls use `--border-strong` (3:1).\n- Disabled controls are exempt under WCAG 1.4.3, but they still get a non-color cue (reduced weight plus a \"not available\" affordance such as a dashed outline), not color alone.\n- `--secondary` is a fill. It is never used as text or as a lone border.\n\n## Chosen system\n\nCandidate A, tuned seed indigo. Inter variable for display and body: `@fontsource-variable/inter` 5.3.0 (CSS family name `'Inter Variable'`). Candidate A is Inter only (user reply \"A\"), so there is no display face and no second family (DSN-04 allows at most 2). Personality is carried by weight, size contrast, tight tracking at display sizes, and motion rather than a second typeface. If a display face is wanted later, candidates B and C record the display faces explored (Fraunces, Bricolage Grotesque) with their Fontsource package names, and the swap is one `--font-display` line plus one package.\n\n- Import: `@fontsource-variable/inter/wght.css` in `main.tsx` (declares `font-display: swap`; per-script `unicode-range` so English copy fetches only the 48 kB latin woff2).\n- Axis range used: weight 400 to 700 only (400 body, 500 UI labels and nav, 600 headings, 700 display). The `opsz` axis file is not imported.\n- Fallback stacks: `--font-sans: 'Inter Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif`; `--font-display` is the same stack. Monospace for code or the email address if needed: `ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace` (system, no package).\n- Type-scale ratio: 1.200 (minor third, from the realtimecolors presets 1.067 to 1.618), base 1rem. `--text-sm` is a half-step (0.9rem) for dense UI copy; the other steps are powers of 1.2.\n\nLadder (`--text-xs` through `--text-5xl`). Sizes 3xl to 5xl are fluid: `clamp(min, intercept + slope vw, max)` interpolates linearly from the 375 px viewport (23.4375rem) to the 1280 px viewport (80rem). The rem part of each clamp keeps browser text zoom effective (WCAG 1.4.4).\n\n| Token | Size | Line height | Notes |\n|-------|------|-------------|-------|\n| `--text-xs` | 0.833rem | 1.5 | Captions, chip labels (never below this) |\n| `--text-sm` | 0.9rem | 1.5 | Dates, card metadata, nav labels |\n| `--text-base` | 1rem | 1.6 | Body copy |\n| `--text-lg` | 1.2rem | 1.5 | Lead paragraphs, summary line |\n| `--text-xl` | 1.44rem | 1.4 | Card titles |\n| `--text-2xl` | 1.728rem | 1.3 | Section sub-headings |\n| `--text-3xl` | clamp(2.074rem, 1.9025rem + 0.732vw, 2.488rem) | 1.2 | Section headings |\n| `--text-4xl` | clamp(2.488rem, 2.034rem + 1.936vw, 3.583rem) | 1.1 | Large section titles |\n| `--text-5xl` | clamp(2.986rem, 2.085rem + 3.844vw, 5.16rem) | 1.05 | Hero display; tracking -0.02em |\n\nCheck points: at 375 px the clamps resolve to 2.074rem, 2.488rem and 2.986rem; at 1280 px to 2.488rem, 3.583rem and 5.16rem. Body copy stays at 1rem on every viewport.\n\n## Spacing, radius, elevation, z-index and breakpoints\n\n- Spacing: Tailwind v4 default base `--spacing: 0.25rem`; all spacing uses the default scale (no custom steps). Minimum touch target 44 by 44 px (`size-11`) for interactive controls.\n- Radius: `--radius-sm: 0.5rem`, `--radius-md: 0.875rem`, `--radius-lg: 1.5rem`, `--radius-pill: 9999px`. Cards use md, the project overlay and large bands use lg, chips and the pill nav use pill.\n- Elevation (per theme, set on `:root` and `[data-theme=dark]`; shadows are decorative, so they carry no contrast requirement; edges that matter use `--border` or `--border-strong`):\n\n| Token | Light | Dark |\n|-------|-------|------|\n| `--shadow-sm` | `0 1px 2px color-mix(in oklch, var(--text) 10%, transparent)` | `0 1px 2px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.5)` |\n| `--shadow-md` | `0 4px 12px color-mix(in oklch, var(--text) 12%, transparent)` | `0 4px 12px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.55)` |\n| `--shadow-lg` | `0 12px 32px color-mix(in oklch, var(--text) 16%, transparent)` | `0 12px 32px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.65)` |\n\n- z-index layers (`--z-*`): base 0, rail-lift 10, sticky-nav 40, pill-nav 50, overlay-backdrop 60, overlay 70, toast 80, skip-link 90. The page order is in the next section.\n12\t\n13\t| Anchor | Section |\n14\t|--------|---------|\n15\t| {#hero} | Hero |\n16\t| {#experience} | Experience |\n17\t| {#projects} | Projects |\n18\t| {#about} | About Me |\n19\t| {#skills} | Skills |\n20\t| {#education} | Education |\n21\t| {#contact} | Contact Me |\n22\t\n23\t## Section order\n24\t\n25\t| Order | Section | Anchor | Why here |\n26\t|-------|---------|--------|----------|\n27\t| 1 | Hero | {#hero} | Name, role and the Resume and Copy email CTAs are visible at first paint, which is most of the 10-second test. |\n28\t| 2 | Experience | {#experience} | Recruiters look for experience first; it is the first thing below the fold and one pill tap from anywhere. |\n29\t| 3 | Projects | {#projects} | The signature rail and overlay; it follows Experience so the work sits next to the roles it came from. |\n30\t| 4 | About Me | {#about} | Personality (the DJ side) comes after the evidence, and links to the Instagram in Contact. |\n31\t| 5 | Skills | {#skills} | A scan-friendly summary once the reader knows the work. |\n32\t| 6 | Education | {#education} | Short, factual, needed for the GPA and degree check, but rarely the first stop. |\n33\t| 7 | Contact Me | {#contact} | The page ends on the action; it is also one tap from the hero CTA and the pill nav. |\n34\t\n35\t## Navigation model\n36\t\n37\t- Below 768 px a thumb-reachable bottom pill nav is fixed to the viewport. Collapsed, it has three segments: Experience, Projects and Menu. Experience and Projects jump straight to their section; the Menu segment morphs the pill in place into a panel of the six section links, the theme toggle and Resume [IX-07] (reference 445). Contact is one tap from the hero CTA and the Contact link in the panel.\n38\t- 768 px and wider use a sticky top nav: section links, the theme toggle [IX-10] and a Resume button, with a scroll-spy indicator under the active link [IX-08]. The bottom pill is not shown at this width.\n39\t- A skip link is the first focusable element and targets {#main}.\n40\t- Nav form is chosen by width. Hover effects are chosen by pointer capability, never by width.\n41\t- Nav links are plain anchors in a single page: there is no router, and the URL changes only by the browser's own hash handling.\n42\t\n43\t## Recruiter fast path (10-second test)\n44\t\n45\tA first-time visitor on a 375 px phone reaches each item with at most one tap from the first viewport.\n46\t\n47\t| Item | Where at 375 | Taps from first viewport |\n48\t|------|--------------|--------------------------|\n49\t| Name | The h1 in the hero, visible on first paint | 0 |\n50\t| Role | The role line directly under the name | 0 |\n51\t| Experience | The Experience segment of the collapsed pill nav | 1 |\n52\t| Projects | The Projects segment of the collapsed pill nav | 1 |\n53\t| Resume | The Download resume CTA in the hero | 1 |\n54\t| Contact | The Contact CTA in the hero, or the Copy email CTA | 1 |\n55\t\n56\tPass rule: all six found in 10 seconds or less, timed on a real phone with motion enabled (the same rule as the design brief).\n57\t\n58\t## Above the fold @ 375\n59\t\n60\tA 375 x 667 viewport shows, top to bottom:\n61\t\n62\t- The name as the h1.\n63\t- The role line under it, with the text effect [IX-01] on the role line only.\n64\t- The Download resume and Copy email CTAs (and a Contact link), each at least 44 px tall.\n65\t- The collapsed pill nav fixed at the bottom, clear of the CTAs.\n66\t- The top edge of {#experience}, so the reader knows there is more below.\n67\t\n68\tThe frame is `### Frame: Hero @ 375`. Nothing in the first viewport depends on JavaScript or motion.\n69\t\n70\t## Anchors and landmarks\n71\t\n72\t- Landmarks: header (skip link and nav), nav, main {#main}, footer.\n73\t- One h1 per page: the name in the hero. Every other section has one h2, and each section element is labelled by its heading with `aria-labelledby`.\n74\t- Section anchors are the seven in the registry above; nav links and CTAs are plain `<a href=\"#anchor\">`.\n75\t- Each section carries `scroll-margin-top` equal to the sticky nav height at 768 px and up, and the height of the safe top area at 375, so a link jump never hides a heading.\n76\t\n77\t## Project rail and overlay behavior\n78\t\n79\tFeatured order: PRJ-01, PRJ-02, PRJ-03, then PRJ-04, PRJ-05, PRJ-06, PRJ-07 (the remaining projects, newest first).\n80\t\n81\t- The rail is native horizontal scrolling with scroll-snap on touch [IX-04] and a hover lift with neighbor shift on a fine pointer [IX-03], with the same lift on keyboard focus [IX-06].\n82\t- Opening a project shows an overlay with the index written as NN / 07. Prev and next wrap around (07 / 07 goes to 01 / 07). The overlay has a Close button; Escape closes it; focus returns to the rail item that opened it; the URL does not change (deep-linkable project URLs are a deferred requirement).\n83\t- Dialog accessibility is settled by ADR-0006: focus trap, inert background, scroll lock and focus return belong to the dialog primitive, and motion animates only the morph [IX-05].\n84\t- Project links and images are deferred (G-01, G-02), so overlay links show only when supplied and rail cards use a cover placeholder.\n85\t\n86\t## Global behaviors\n87\t\n88\t- Press-squish [IX-02] on all buttons and cards, on the inner surface only.\n89\t- Section reveals [IX-15] when a section enters the viewport; content is visible by default and the hidden start state is set after mount.\n90\t- Desktop smooth wheel scroll [IX-16], off on touch and under reduced motion.\n91\t- Desktop pointer polish [IX-17]: Tilt on the About photo, Magnetic on the hero and contact CTA wrappers, Spotlight on experience cards, fine pointer only.\n92\t\n93\t## Frame conventions\n94\t\n95\t- Frames are drawn in a fenced `text` block with printable ASCII only. The width counts the whole line including both `|` borders: 38 characters for 375 px, 64 for 768 px and 96 for 1280 px (so the inner width is 36, 62 and 94).\n96\t- Square-bracket annotations name an interaction ID from `01-MOTION-SPEC.md` (for example [IX-09]) or an anchor (for example [#contact]).\n97\t- `[ Label ]` is a button. `Label >` is a link. `(( ))` marks the toast. `=====` borders the bottom pill nav and its expanded panel on mobile. `#` borders mark a visible focus ring. `:::` marks a blurred backdrop. `( )` around a word is a chip, `[logo]` and `[ O ]` are logo and monogram chips.\n98\t- Touch targets are at least 44 px high and wide at 375 px.\n99\t- The fixed bottom pill is drawn only where it matters (Hero, Contact, the nav states); the sticky top nav is drawn in the Hero frames and the nav state frames. Dates in frames use an ASCII hyphen; on the site they are written with an en dash per the date policy in the inventory.\n100\t- Copy in frames is abbreviated where it does not fit (for example short month names at 375). The full copy is in `01-CONTENT-INVENTORY.md`.\n101\t\n102\t## Wireframes\n103\t\n104\t### Frame: Hero @ 375\n105\t\n106\tThe first viewport (375 x 667): name, role line, three CTAs in the HERO-03 order, the collapsed pill nav and the top edge of Experience. Plan 01-07 set the final section order and added the hero, nav, rail, overlay and every other section at 375, 768 and 1280 px.\n\nWireframes are ASCII inside this markdown file (D-02). No HTML sketches.\n\n## Section registry\n\nSeven fixed anchors. Every phase doc refers to a section by its anchor, never by a position number. The page order is in the next section.\n\n| Anchor | Section |\n|--------|---------|\n| {#hero} | Hero |\n| {#experience} | Experience |\n| {#projects} | Projects |\n| {#about} | About Me |\n| {#skills} | Skills |\n| {#education} | Education |\n| {#contact} | Contact Me |\n\n## Section order\n\n| Order | Section | Anchor | Why here |\n|-------|---------|--------|----------|\n| 1 | Hero | {#hero} | Name, role and the Resume and Copy email CTAs are visible at first paint, which is most of the 10-second test. |\n| 2 | Experience | {#experience} | Recruiters look for experience first; it is the first thing below the fold and one pill tap from anywhere. |\n| 3 | Projects | {#projects} | The signature rail and overlay; it follows Experience so the work sits next to the roles it came from. |\n| 4 | About Me | {#about} | Personality (the DJ side) comes after the evidence, and links to the Instagram in Contact. |\n| 5 | Skills | {#skills} | A scan-friendly summary once the reader knows the work. |\n| 6 | Education | {#education} | Short, factual, needed for the GPA and degree check, but rarely the first stop. |\n| 7 | Contact Me | {#contact} | The page ends on the action; it is also one tap from the hero CTA and the pill nav. |\n\n## Navigation model\n\n- Below 768 px a thumb-reachable bottom pill nav is fixed to the viewport. Collapsed, it has three segments: Experience, Projects and Menu. Experience and Projects jump straight to their section; the Menu segment morphs the pill in place into a panel of the six section links, the theme toggle and Resume [IX-07] (reference 445). Contact is one tap from the hero CTA and the Contact link in the panel.\n- 768 px and wider use a sticky top nav: section links, the theme toggle [IX-10] and a Resume button, with a scroll-spy indicator under the active link [IX-08]. The bottom pill is not shown at this width.\n- A skip link is the first focusable element and targets {#main}.\n- Nav form is chosen by width. Hover effects are chosen by pointer capability, never by width.\n- Nav links are plain anchors in a single page: there is no router, and the URL changes only by the browser's own hash handling.\n\n## Recruiter fast path (10-second test)\n\nA first-time visitor on a 375 px phone reaches each item with at most one tap from the first viewport.\n\n| Item | Where at 375 | Taps from first viewport |\n|------|--------------|--------------------------|\n| Name | The h1 in the hero, visible on first paint | 0 |\n| Role | The role line directly under the name | 0 |\n| Experience | The Experience segment of the collapsed pill nav | 1 |\n| Projects | The Projects segment of the collapsed pill nav | 1 |\n| Resume | The Download resume CTA in the hero | 1 |\n| Contact | The Contact CTA in the hero, or the Copy email CTA | 1 |\n\nPass rule: all six found in 10 seconds or less, timed on a real phone with motion enabled (the same rule as the design brief).\n\n## Above the fold @ 375\n\nA 375 x 667 viewport shows, top to bottom:\n\n- The name as the h1.\n- The role line under it, with the text effect [IX-01] on the role line only.\n- The Download resume and Copy email CTAs (and a Contact link), each at least 44 px tall.\n- The collapsed pill nav fixed at the bottom, clear of the CTAs.\n- The top edge of {#experience}, so the reader knows there is more below.\n\nThe frame is `### Frame: Hero @ 375`. Nothing in the first viewport depends on JavaScript or motion.\n\n## Anchors and landmarks\n\n- Landmarks: header (skip link and nav), nav, main {#main}, footer.\n- One h1 per page: the name in the hero. Every other section has one h2, and each section element is labelled by its heading with `aria-labelledby`.\n- Section anchors are the seven in the registry above; nav links and CTAs are plain `<a href=\"#anchor\">`.\n- Each section carries `scroll-margin-top` equal to the sticky nav height at 768 px and up, and the height of the safe top area at 375, so a link jump never hides a heading.\n\n## Project rail and overlay behavior\n\nFeatured order: PRJ-01, PRJ-02, PRJ-03, then PRJ-04, PRJ-05, PRJ-06, PRJ-07 (the remaining projects, newest first).\n\n- The rail is native horizontal scrolling with scroll-snap on touch [IX-04] and a hover lift with neighbor shift on a fine pointer [IX-03], with the same lift on keyboard focus [IX-06].\n- Opening a project shows an overlay with the index written as NN / 07. Prev and next wrap around (07 / 07 goes to 01 / 07). The overlay has a Close button; Escape closes it; focus returns to the rail item that opened it; the URL does not change (deep-linkable project URLs are a deferred requirement).\n- Dialog accessibility is settled by ADR-0006: focus trap, inert background, scroll lock and focus return belong to the dialog primitive, and motion animates only the morph [IX-05].\n- Project links and images are deferred (G-01, G-02), so overlay links show only when supplied and rail cards use a cover placeholder.\n\n## Global behaviors\n\n- Press-squish [IX-02] on all buttons and cards, on the inner surface only.\n- Section reveals [IX-15] when a section enters the viewport; content is visible by default and the hidden start state is set after mount.\n- Desktop smooth wheel scroll [IX-16], off on touch and under reduced motion.\n- Desktop pointer polish [IX-17]: Tilt on the About photo, Magnetic on the hero and contact CTA wrappers, Spotlight on experience cards, fine pointer only.\n\n## Frame conventions\n\n- Frames are drawn in a fenced `text` block with printable ASCII only. The width counts the whole line including both `|` borders: 38 characters for 375 px, 64 for 768 px and 96 for 1280 px (so the inner width is 36, 62 and 94).\n- Square-bracket annotations name an interaction ID from `01-MOTION-SPEC.md` (for example [IX-09]) or an anchor (for example [#contact]).\n- `[ Label ]` is a button. `Label >` is a link. `(( ))` marks the toast. `=====` borders the bottom pill nav and its expanded panel on mobile. `#` borders mark a visible focus ring. `:::` marks a blurred backdrop. `( )` around a word is a chip, `[logo]` and `[ O ]` are logo and monogram chips.\n- Touch targets are at least 44 px high and wide at 375 px.\n- The fixed bottom pill is drawn only where it matters (Hero, Contact, the nav states); the sticky top nav is drawn in the Hero frames and the nav state frames. Dates in frames use an ASCII hyphen; on the site they are written with an en dash per the date policy in the inventory.\n- Copy in frames is abbreviated where it does not fit (for example short month names at 375). The full copy is in `01-CONTENT-INVENTORY.md`.\n\n## Wireframes\n\n### Frame: Hero @ 375\n\nThe first viewport (375 x 667): name, role line, three CTAs in the HERO-03 order, the collapsed pill nav and the top edge of Experience. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Njganrs2WYDDVnm3U876tV","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Motion Spec (DOC-05)\n2\t\n3\tStatus: Accepted\n4\t\n5\tPhase 1 plan 01-01 seeded this file with the ownership rule, the fixed 17-row interaction catalog and the first fully specified interaction (IX-09). Plan 01-05 completed it: principles, tokens, reduced-motion layers, ownership matrix, vendored primitives, the other 16 interaction specs and the element ownership check.\n6\t\n7\t## Ownership rule\n8\t\n9\t- Exactly one library animates any element: motion, react-spring, CSS or Lenis. Never two on the same element or property.\n10\t- No Tailwind transition utilities on an element a library animates.\n11\t- react-spring is scoped to IX-02, IX-03, IX-06 and IX-10 (velocity-carrying, tactile physics). Everything else uses motion, CSS or Lenis as the catalog says.\n12\t\n13\t## Principles\n14\t\n15\t- Motion never gates content. Name, role and CTAs are visible at first paint. The hero text effect runs only on the role line and never delays it.\n16\t- Animate transform and opacity only, plus motion layout animations where an interaction needs them (IX-05, IX-07, IX-08, IX-11, IX-14).\n17\t- Fine-pointer effects are gated by the media query `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` and carry no hover-only content (MOT-04). Touch gets a tap or press equivalent, or nothing.\n18\t- `touch-action` is set only on small draggables. The project rail uses native horizontal scrolling, so vertical page scroll is never captured.\n19\t- Infinite or looping motion pauses when off-screen or when the tab is hidden.\n20\t- Motion budget: entrance animations take at most 420 ms; stagger is at most 60 ms per item for at most 6 items; nothing blocks input.\n21\t\n22\t## Motion tokens\n23\t\n24\tCanonical home is `src/anim/tokens.ts`, with CSS mirrors `--dur-fast`, `--dur-base`, `--dur-slow` and `--ease-out`. One table drives both libraries so they feel like one system.\n25\t\n26\t| Token | Kind | motion format (stiffness, damping, mass) | react-spring format (tension, friction, mass) | Value |\n27\t|-------|------|------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|-------|\n28\t| snappy | spring | 500, 32, 1 | 500, 32, 1 | presses, toggles |\n29\t| gentle | spring | 170, 26, 1 | 170, 26, 1 | rail lift, layout settling |\n30\t| bouncy | spring | 300, 14, 1 | 300, 14, 1 | playful overshoot, used sparingly |\n31\t| fast | duration | n/a | n/a | 120 ms |\n32\t| base | duration | n/a | n/a | 220 ms |\n33\t| slow | duration | n/a | n/a | 420 ms |\n34\t| ease-out | easing | n/a | n/a | cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) |\n35\t\n36\treact-spring `tension` equals motion `stiffness` and `friction` equals `damping`. The spring numbers are starting values, to be tuned on a real iPhone and a real Android phone during the signature-rail work (Phase 4).\n37\t\n38\t## Reduced motion\n39\t\n40\tOne preference source (MOT-01): `useMotionPreference` reads `prefers-reduced-motion` with a `change` listener (users toggle it live) and feeds three consumers:\n41\t\n42\t- motion: `MotionConfig` `reducedMotion` (from `motion/react`).\n43\t- react-spring: `Globals.assign({ skipAnimation })` from `@react-spring/web`, set in an effect with a dependency array and a cleanup that resets it.\n44\t- CSS: the guard `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, which also gates smooth scroll behind `no-preference`.\n45\t\n46\tLenis is not started under reduced motion (MOT-05). Motion's `user` mode still animates opacity, so text effects and other opacity-driven wrappers branch manually on the hook's `reduced` value.\n47\t\n48\t| Layer | Mechanism | Covers |\n49\t|-------|-----------|--------|\n50\t| L0 Progressive enhancement | Content is visible by default in HTML and CSS. Reveal wrappers set the hidden initial state only after mount on the client, and `<noscript>` guarantees visibility. | JS failure, slow hydration, crawlers, screenshots |\n51\t| L1 CSS guard | `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` collapses animation and transition durations to near zero, runs animations once and sets `scroll-behavior: auto`. | CSS transitions, keyframes, anchor scroll |\n52\t| L2 motion | `MotionConfig` `reducedMotion` (\"user\", or \"always\" and \"never\" from an override). Disables transform and layout animations, keeps opacity and color. | All motion components, including vendored primitives |\n53\t| L3 react-spring | `Globals.assign({ skipAnimation })` in the provider effect. Springs jump to their target. | All spring physics |\n54\t| L4 Wrapper branches | Wrappers branch on `reduced` to drop parallax and scroll-linked transforms, stop loops and autoplay (text loop, infinite slider), disable fling, and swap transforms for short fades or nothing. | What L2 and L3 do not cover |\n55\t| L5 Non-motion feedback | Pressed, focus and selected states read without motion, through color, outline or shape. | Reduced-motion users still get feedback |\n56\t| L6 Visible toggle | Optional \"Reduce motion\" control persisted to localStorage and fed into `useMotionPreference`. Open decision, not committed. | Users whose OS setting is off but who want calm |\n57\t\n58\t## Ownership matrix\n59\t\n60\tMOT-02. Every interaction class has exactly one owner.\n61\t\n62\t| Interaction class | Owner | Why |\n63\t|-------------------|-------|-----|\n64\t| Mount, unmount and presence | motion (`AnimatePresence`) | Mature exit handling under React 19 |\n65\t| Layout and shared-element morphs | motion (`layout`, `layoutId`) | react-spring has no equivalent |\n66\t| Scroll-linked values and in-view reveals | motion (`useScroll`, `whileInView`) | Already bundled |\n67\t| Text and number effects, motion-primitives prefabs | motion | The primitives are written against it |\n68\t| Velocity physics, press-squish, rail lift with neighbor shift, theme toggle thumb | react-spring (`useSpring`, `useSprings`) | Continuous retargeting gives the tactile signature |\n69\t| Color and hover transitions, native scroll-snap rail | CSS | Zero JS cost |\n70\t| Desktop wheel smoothing | Lenis | Wheel only, off on touch |\n71\t\n72\tConstraints:\n73\t\n74\t- Install `@react-spring/web` at `~10.1.x` only; never the umbrella `react-spring` package.\n75\t- Avoid `useTransition` in core UI; presence is motion's job, which keeps the react-spring v11 migration trivial.\n76\t- `@use-gesture/react` is not added up front.\n77\t- Import motion only from `motion/react`, never raw `framer-motion`.\n78\t- Whether react-spring stays at all is decided after the rail is measured (bundle cost and feel).\n79\t\n80\t## Vendored motion-primitives\n81\t\n82\tCopied in as owned source under `src/components/motion-primitives/`, not installed from npm.\n83\t\n84\t| Component | Used for | Notes |\n85\t|-----------|----------|-------|\n86\t| TextEffect or TextLoop | IX-01 | Role line only |\n87\t| MorphingDialog | IX-05 | Adoption is subject to the overlay accessibility ADR and its spike |\n88\t| AnimatedNumber with InView | IX-12 | Once |\n89\t| InfiniteSlider | IX-13 | Pauses off-screen, on focus and hover, and when the tab is hidden |\n90\t| Tilt, Magnetic, Spotlight | IX-17 | Fine pointer only |\n91\t\n92\tNot vendored: Cursor, Dock and any other mouse-only primitive.
