Plan 01-05 completed it: principles, tokens, reduced-motion layers, ownership matrix, vendored primitives, the other 16 interaction specs and the element ownership check.\n\n## Ownership rule\n\n- Exactly one library animates any element: motion, react-spring, CSS or Lenis. Never two on the same element or property.\n- No Tailwind transition utilities on an element a library animates.\n- react-spring is scoped to IX-02, IX-03, IX-06 and IX-10 (velocity-carrying, tactile physics). Everything else uses motion, CSS or Lenis as the catalog says.\n\n## Principles\n\n- Motion never gates content. Name, role and CTAs are visible at first paint. The hero text effect runs only on the role line and never delays it.\n- Animate transform and opacity only, plus motion layout animations where an interaction needs them (IX-05, IX-07, IX-08, IX-11, IX-14).\n- Fine-pointer effects are gated by the media query `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` and carry no hover-only content (MOT-04). Touch gets a tap or press equivalent, or nothing.\n- `touch-action` is set only on small draggables. The project rail uses native horizontal scrolling, so vertical page scroll is never captured.\n- Infinite or looping motion pauses when off-screen or when the tab is hidden.\n- Motion budget: entrance animations take at most 420 ms; stagger is at most 60 ms per item for at most 6 items; nothing blocks input.\n\n## Motion tokens\n\nCanonical home is `src/anim/tokens.ts`, with CSS mirrors `--dur-fast`, `--dur-base`, `--dur-slow` and `--ease-out`. One table drives both libraries so they feel like one system.\n\n| Token | Kind | motion format (stiffness, damping, mass) | react-spring format (tension, friction, mass) | Value |\n|-------|------|------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|-------|\n| snappy | spring | 500, 32, 1 | 500, 32, 1 | presses, toggles |\n| gentle | spring | 170, 26, 1 | 170, 26, 1 | rail lift, layout settling |\n| bouncy | spring | 300, 14, 1 | 300, 14, 1 | playful overshoot, used sparingly |\n| fast | duration | n/a | n/a | 120 ms |\n| base | duration | n/a | n/a | 220 ms |\n| slow | duration | n/a | n/a | 420 ms |\n| ease-out | easing | n/a | n/a | cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) |\n\nreact-spring `tension` equals motion `stiffness` and `friction` equals `damping`. The spring numbers are starting values, to be tuned on a real iPhone and a real Android phone during the signature-rail work (Phase 4).\n\n## Reduced motion\n\nOne preference source (MOT-01): `useMotionPreference` reads `prefers-reduced-motion` with a `change` listener (users toggle it live) and feeds three consumers:\n\n- motion: `MotionConfig` `reducedMotion` (from `motion/react`).\n- react-spring: `Globals.assign({ skipAnimation })` from `@react-spring/web`, set in an effect with a dependency array and a cleanup that resets it.\n- CSS: the guard `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, which also gates smooth scroll behind `no-preference`.\n\nLenis is not started under reduced motion (MOT-05). Motion's `user` mode still animates opacity, so text effects and other opacity-driven wrappers branch manually on the hook's `reduced` value.\n\n| Layer | Mechanism | Covers |\n|-------|-----------|--------|\n| L0 Progressive enhancement | Content is visible by default in HTML and CSS. Reveal wrappers set the hidden initial state only after mount on the client, and `<noscript>` guarantees visibility. | JS failure, slow hydration, crawlers, screenshots |\n| L1 CSS guard | `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` collapses animation and transition durations to near zero, runs animations once and sets `scroll-behavior: auto`. | CSS transitions, keyframes, anchor scroll |\n| L2 motion | `MotionConfig` `reducedMotion` (\"user\", or \"always\" and \"never\" from an override). Disables transform and layout animations, keeps opacity and color. | All motion components, including vendored primitives |\n| L3 react-spring | `Globals.assign({ skipAnimation })` in the provider effect. Springs jump to their target. | All spring physics |\n| L4 Wrapper branches | Wrappers branch on `reduced` to drop parallax and scroll-linked transforms, stop loops and autoplay (text loop, infinite slider), disable fling, and swap transforms for short fades or nothing. | What L2 and L3 do not cover |\n| L5 Non-motion feedback | Pressed, focus and selected states read without motion, through color, outline or shape. | Reduced-motion users still get feedback |\n| L6 Visible toggle | Optional \"Reduce motion\" control persisted to localStorage and fed into `useMotionPreference`. Open decision, not committed. | Users whose OS setting is off but who want calm |\n\n## Ownership matrix\n\nMOT-02. Every interaction class has exactly one owner.\n\n| Interaction class | Owner | Why |\n|-------------------|-------|-----|\n| Mount, unmount and presence | motion (`AnimatePresence`) | Mature exit handling under React 19 |\n| Layout and shared-element morphs | motion (`layout`, `layoutId`) | react-spring has no equivalent |\n| Scroll-linked values and in-view reveals | motion (`useScroll`, `whileInView`) | Already bundled |\n| Text and number effects, motion-primitives prefabs | motion | The primitives are written against it |\n| Velocity physics, press-squish, rail lift with neighbor shift, theme toggle thumb | react-spring (`useSpring`, `useSprings`) | Continuous retargeting gives the tactile signature |\n| Color and hover transitions, native scroll-snap rail | CSS | Zero JS cost |\n| Desktop wheel smoothing | Lenis | Wheel only, off on touch |\n\nConstraints:\n\n- Install `@react-spring/web` at `~10.1.x` only; never the umbrella `react-spring` package.\n- Avoid `useTransition` in core UI; presence is motion's job, which keeps the react-spring v11 migration trivial.\n- `@use-gesture/react` is not added up front.\n- Import motion only from `motion/react`, never raw `framer-motion`.\n- Whether react-spring stays at all is decided after the rail is measured (bundle cost and feel).\n\n## Vendored motion-primitives\n\nCopied in as owned source under `src/components/motion-primitives/`, not installed from npm.\n\n| Component | Used for | Notes |\n|-----------|----------|-------|\n| TextEffect or TextLoop | IX-01 | Role line only |\n| MorphingDialog | IX-05 | Adoption is subject to the overlay accessibility ADR and its spike |\n| AnimatedNumber with InView | IX-12 | Once |\n| InfiniteSlider | IX-13 | Pauses off-screen, on focus and hover, and when the tab is hidden |\n| Tilt, Magnetic, Spotlight | IX-17 | Fine pointer only |\n\nNot vendored: Cursor, Dock and any other mouse-only primitive. Each vendored file is patched for type-only imports and gets a reduced-motion branch.\n\n## Interaction catalog index\n\nThe 17 IDs below are fixed. Wireframes annotate with them and the motion plan fills them in.\n\n| ID | Interaction | Section | Requirement | Owner |\n|----|-------------|---------|-------------|-------|\n| IX-01 | Hero role-line text effect | {#hero} | SEC-04 | motion |\n| IX-02 | Press-squish on buttons and cards | global | MOT-03 | react-spring |\n| IX-03 | Rail hover lift and neighbor shift | {#projects} | SIG-01 MOT-04 | react-spring |\n| IX-04 | Rail swipe on touch | {#projects} | SIG-02 | CSS |\n| IX-05 | Project overlay open, close, prev/next | {#projects} | SIG-03 | motion |\n| IX-06 | Rail keyboard focus lift | {#projects} | SIG-04 | react-spring |\n| IX-07 | Mobile morphing pill nav | global | NAV-02 | motion |\n| IX-08 | Desktop sticky nav scroll-spy indicator | global | NAV-02 | motion |\n| IX-09 | Copy-email confirmation toast | {#contact} | NAV-03 | motion |\n| IX-10 | Theme toggle thumb | global | DSN-03 | react-spring |\n| IX-11 | Experience card expand and collapse | {#experience} | SEC-01 | motion |\n| IX-12 | Experience metric count-up | {#experience} | SEC-01 | motion |\n| IX-13 | Skills slider strip | {#skills} | SEC-02 | motion |\n| IX-14 | Education card expand or flip | {#education} | SEC-03 | motion |\n| IX-15 | Section in-view reveal | all sections | MOT-01 | motion |\n| IX-16 | Desktop smooth wheel scroll | global | MOT-05 | Lenis |\n| IX-17 | Desktop pointer polish (Tilt on the About photo, Magnetic on CTA wrappers, Spotlight on experience cards) | {#hero} {#about} {#experience} {#contact} | MOT-04 | motion |\n\n## Interactions\n\nEach interaction is a subsection of bullet lines in the form `- Label: value`, with the 12 labels in this order: Section, Trigger, Element, Owner library, API, Properties, Token, Touch equivalent, Keyboard path, Reduced-motion fallback, Requirement, Build phase.\n\n### IX-01 Hero role-line text effect\n\n- Section: {#hero}\n- Trigger: on mount, once the role line is in view\n- Element: the role line only; the name, the CTAs and the rest of the hero are never animated by this effect\n- Owner library: motion\n- API: motion-primitives TextEffect or TextLoop\n- Properties: opacity and translateY per word or character, within the 420 ms entrance budget\n- Token: duration slow 420 ms, ease-out; stagger at most 60 ms per item for at most 6 items\n- Touch equivalent: none needed, runs without input\n- Keyboard path: none needed, not interactive; screen readers get the full role text through the element's text or an aria-label, never per-character spans\n- Reduced-motion fallback: the static full role line is rendered immediately, with no loop and no per-character animation\n- Requirement: SEC-04\n- Build phase: 4\n\n### IX-02 Press-squish on buttons and cards\n\n- Section: global\n- Trigger: pointerdown and pointerup on buttons and cards, and Enter or Space keydown and keyup on focused buttons\n- Element: the inner button or card surface (for CTAs, the inner button inside the Magnetic wrapper)\n- Owner library: react-spring\n- API: useSpring on an animated element\n- Properties: transform scale only (about 0.96 pressed)\n- Token: spring snappy\n- Touch equivalent: pointerdown and pointerup are the touch events, so a tap squishes the same way\n- Keyboard path: native buttons; Enter and Space keydown and keyup drive the same spring\n- Reduced-motion fallback: no scale; the pressed state is shown by color or shade change (L5)\n- Requirement: MOT-03\n- Build phase: 4\n\n### IX-03 Rail hover lift and neighbor shift\n\n- Section: {#projects}\n- Trigger: pointer hover over a rail item, active only under (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)\n- Element: the outer rail item and its neighbors\n- Owner library: react-spring\n- API: useSprings over the rail items\n- Properties: translateY and translateX (neighbor shift) only\n- Token: spring gentle\n- Touch equivalent: none needed, IX-04 provides the touch path\n- Keyboard path: IX-06 triggers the same lift from :focus-visible\n- Reduced-motion fallback: no lift or shift; the hovered item gets an elevation and outline change instead (L5)\n- Requirement: SIG-01, MOT-04\n- Build phase: 4\n\n### IX-04 Rail swipe on touch\n\n- Section: {#projects}\n- Trigger: horizontal swipe on touch, or trackpad and shift-wheel on desktop; tap on an item opens IX-05\n- Element: the rail scroll container\n- Owner library: CSS\n- API: native horizontal overflow with scroll-snap-type x mandatory and scroll-snap-align on items; no JS animation library\n- Properties: native scroll position only\n- Token: none, native scroll physics\n- Touch equivalent: this is the touch path; vertical page scroll stays untouched because no touch-action is set on the rail\n- Keyboard path: the container and items are focusable; arrow keys move between items (see IX-06) and the browser scrolls the focused item into view\n- Reduced-motion fallback: unchanged because the motion is user-driven; scroll-behavior stays auto\n- Requirement: SIG-02\n- Build phase: 4\n\n### IX-05 Project overlay open, close, prev/next\n\n- Section: {#projects}\n- Trigger: tap, click, or Enter on a rail item; close by close button, backdrop or Escape; prev/next by buttons or arrow keys\n- Element: the inner card element of the rail item (layoutId source) and the overlay panel (layoutId target), plus the blurred backdrop\n- Owner library: motion\n- API: AnimatePresence plus a shared layoutId morph from the rail item's inner card element; prev/next crossfade; index shown as \"NN / 07\"\n- Properties: layout transform, opacity and backdrop blur\n- Token: spring gentle for the morph, duration base 220 ms for the crossfade and backdrop\n- Touch equivalent: tap opens, backdrop tap or close button closes, previous and next buttons replace arrow keys\n- Keyboard path: focus trap, Escape and focus return to the originating rail item come from the dialog primitive chosen by the overlay accessibility ADR, not from motion\n- Reduced-motion fallback: instant open and close with no morph and no blur transition\n- Requirement: SIG-03\n- Build phase: 4\n\n### IX-06 Rail keyboard focus lift\n\n- Section: {#projects}\n- Trigger: :focus-visible on a rail item\n- Element: the outer rail item and its neighbors, the same elements as IX-03\n- Owner library: react-spring\n- API: the same useSprings instance as IX-03, driven by focus-visible state\n- Properties: translateY and translateX only\n- Token: spring gentle\n- Touch equivalent: none needed, IX-04 provides the touch path and focus-visible does not fire on tap\n- Keyboard path: arrow keys move between items, Enter opens IX-05\n- Reduced-motion fallback: outline only, no lift\n- Requirement: SIG-04\n- Build phase: 4\n\n### IX-07 Mobile morphing pill nav\n\n- Section: global\n- Trigger: tap on the Menu segment of the bottom pill below 768 px (the Experience and Projects segments are plain anchors that jump straight to their sections)\n- Element: the bottom pill, which expands in place into a frosted panel (reference 445)\n- Owner library: motion\n- API: layout animation on the pill and panel container, AnimatePresence for the panel content\n- Properties: layout transform and opacity\n- Token: spring gentle\n- Touch equivalent: tap to expand, tap a link or the close button to collapse\n- Keyboard path: the pill is a native button with aria-expanded; Escape and a close button collapse it and return focus to the pill\n- Reduced-motion fallback: instant state switch\n- Requirement: NAV-02\n- Build phase: 3 for structure, 4 for motion\n\n### IX-08 Desktop sticky nav scroll-spy indicator\n\n- Section: global\n- Trigger: scrolling a section into the active band, detected with IntersectionObserver; the mobile pill (IX-07) is the nav below 768 px, and a tablet at 768 px or wider taps the same links\n- Keyboard path: nav links are native anchors; Tab and Enter navigate, and the indicator follows the active section\n- Reduced-motion fallback: the indicator jumps to the active link with no slide\n- Requirement: NAV-02\n- Build phase: 3 for structure, 4 for motion\n\n### IX-09 Copy-email confirmation toast\n\n- Section: {#contact}\n- Trigger: tap or click on Copy email, or Enter/Space on the focused button\n- Element: toast region\n- Owner library: motion\n- API: AnimatePresence around the toast\n- Properties: opacity and translateY only\n- Token: duration base 220 ms, ease-out\n- Touch equivalent: tap, same toast\n- Keyboard path: native button; The new site is built by GitHub Actions and first deployed as a staging project site of this repository. `VITE_BASE` is set to `/` plus this repository's name plus `/`, so the staging URL is `https://aa-phan.github.io/aa-phan-portfolio-v2/` and CI catches broken sub-path assets before launch.\n2. The cutover is an additive commit on top of the existing `aa-phan.github.io` history. First the iPod site is tagged (`v1-ipod`) and that tag and a matching branch are pushed, so the old site stays recoverable. Then the iPod files are removed and the new site source is added in a normal commit, merged through a pull request.\n3. The Pages source of `aa-phan.github.io` is switched from the legacy branch source to GitHub Actions in the same sitting as the merge, and the deploy workflow is then triggered with `workflow_dispatch` so the new site goes live immediately.\n4. Force-pushing `aa-phan.github.io` is forbidden, for the cutover and for the rollback.\n5. Private planning files and the private reference folder are not copied into `aa-phan.github.io`. Only the source the site needs, the workflow and `docs/` are.\n\nThe step-by-step procedure, the workflow settings and the smoke test are in the [deploy runbook](../deploy-runbook.md).\n\n## Consequences\n\n- The live site and its history stay recoverable at every point: the old site is a tag, the cutover is one revertible commit, and nothing is rewritten.\n- There may be a short window, while the Pages source is switched, in which the live URL returns a 404. This is possible but unverified (open decision OD-05); the switch and the workflow trigger are done back to back to keep it short.\n- Staging on the project URL proves the Actions pipeline, base-path handling and asset paths before the user-site URL is touched.\n- Staging requires pushing this repository to GitHub, which OD-01 no longer blocks.\n\n## Rollback\n\nIf the new site is broken or the switch goes wrong:\n\n1. In the `aa-phan.github.io` repository settings, set the Pages source back to \"Deploy from a branch\", branch `main`, folder `/`.\n2. Revert the cutover commit with `git revert`, or restore the iPod files from the `v1-ipod` tag with a normal commit.\n3. Never force-push.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n- Replace the repository history with the new site (force-push). Rejected: it destroys the old site's history and the rollback path.\n- Deploy the new site from a built-output branch instead of Actions. Rejected: it keeps build artifacts in git history and loses the CI gates.\n- Keep the iPod site where it is and serve the new site only from the project URL. Rejected: the new site is meant to replace the iPod site at the user-site URL.\n- Rehearse the source switch on a throwaway repository first. Not required; tracked as OD-05 so the owner can choose to accept the unverified downtime with the written rollback.\n\n## Revisit when\n\nAfter the cutover, once the source-switch downtime has been observed (OD-05), or if GitHub changes how Pages sources are switched.\n","numLines":55,"startLine":1,"totalLines":55}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01Km43DiyCxYKo7YStM2ze2o","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

As a modal dialog it must:\n\n1. Trap keyboard focus inside the overlay while it is open.\n2. Close on Escape.\n3. Lock background scroll.\n4. Make the background inert, so assistive technology and tab order cannot reach it.\n5. Return focus to the rail item that opened it.\n6. Expose `role=\"dialog\"` with `aria-modal=\"true\"` and a label taken from the project title.\n7. Keep previous, next and close reachable and usable by keyboard.\n\nThe vendored `MorphingDialog` component from motion-primitives gives the morph animation. Its behavior on the seven points above has not been verified.\n\nThe motion spec splits responsibility the same way: motion animates the overlay, and the dialog primitive owns focus, Escape, inert background and scroll lock.\n\n## Decision\n\nMotion owns the overlay animation: `AnimatePresence` plus a shared `layoutId` morph from the rail item's inner card to the overlay panel, with a crossfade for previous and next. The dialog primitive owns everything on the checklist above: focus trap, Escape, inert background, scroll lock and focus return. The two concerns stay separate.\n\nA code spike checks `MorphingDialog` against the seven-point checklist before the rail ships. The spike itself is deferred to the interaction build (Phase 2 or 4) and is not run as part of the documentation work.\n\n- If every point passes, `MorphingDialog` is used as vendored.\n- If any point fails, the overlay uses a native `dialog` element opened with `showModal()`. Top-layer rendering makes the rest of the page inert and the `cancel` event handles Escape. Focus return and scroll lock are handled explicitly in our code. Motion animates only the inner panel; the `layoutId` morph targets that inner panel rendered inside the `dialog` element, not the `dialog` element itself.\n- Radix Dialog is considered only if both of the above fail, because it adds a dependency.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Overlay animation and overlay accessibility are separate concerns, so either primitive works with the same motion spec and the same reduced-motion fallback (instant open and close, no morph).\n- The native fallback costs a little explicit code (focus return, scroll lock) and no new dependency.\n- With the native fallback, the backdrop blur and the morph are applied to elements inside the `dialog`, because the `dialog` element's own box is not what animates.\n- The rail cannot ship until the spike result is recorded.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n- Adopt `MorphingDialog` without checking it. Rejected: an unverified focus trap and Escape path is an accessibility failure on the site's main interaction.\n- Always use the native `dialog` element. Not chosen as the default only because `MorphingDialog` may already pass and would then be less code; it stays the fallback.\n- Radix Dialog. Held back: it solves the checklist but adds a dependency for one overlay.\n- Build a custom focus trap. Rejected: the native `dialog` element already provides one.\n\n## Revisit when\n\nThe spike result is recorded (open decision OD-06), or if the overlay design changes so it is no longer modal.\n","numLines":50,"startLine":1,"totalLines":50}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01ScPLMwt4uSdmZcv8tTpRuf","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

The role line splits into 13 segments (7 words and the whitespace between), giving about 0.35 s in total, inside the 420 ms entrance budget.\n\nMeasured gzipped sizes (level 9) at adoption:\n\n| Build | Initial JS | Effect chunk |\n|-------|-----------|--------------|\n| Lazy (shipped) | 86,954 B | 49,991 B, requested only after first paint and never under reduced motion |\n| Eager import (measured in the research probe) | about 134.5 kB | none |\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Upstream fixes are pulled by hand: fetch the registry JSON again, review the diff, and record the new hash here or in a superseding ADR.\n- The initial bundle stays about 47 kB gzipped smaller than an eager import would make it.\n- The static role line is in the first paint, then re-reveals for about 0.35 s when the chunk arrives. This is inherent to a reveal effect on text already present in the HTML; whether it reads as intentional on a phone is a taste call settled at review.\n- The 7-word line has 7 stagger steps, more than the 6-item guideline, while staying inside the total time envelope (the whole stagger is about 0.2 s).\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n- The motion-primitives CLI. Rejected: it writes to a repository-root folder and its package is stale.\n- An eager import. Rejected: about 50 kB gzipped more initial JavaScript for a decorative effect.\n- A hand-written word reveal. Rejected: the vendored component already handles the screen-reader copy and hides the per-word fragments from assistive technology.\n\n## Revisit when\n\nThe hero text effect gets its section-treatment polish, `motion` changes major version, or LazyMotion is adopted (open decision OD-03, which can use the bundle numbers recorded above).\n","numLines":43,"startLine":1,"totalLines":43}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_014nSmKCzFQ4Xph8yewRXRzA","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Cq2z7jBrFxfoY6UoUoom2P","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Architecture\n2\t\n3\tStatus: Accepted\n4\t\n5\tThis document describes how the portfolio site is structured: layers, import rules, folder layout, data flow, the content model, the design-token pipeline and the animation layer. It is written so the scaffold can be built directly from it. Decisions with a longer rationale live in the [ADR log](adr/README.md).\n6\t\n7\t## Overview\n8\t\n9\tThe site is a static, zero-backend, single-page React app served from GitHub Pages. There is no router, no global store and no data fetching. The architecture comes down to four seams:\n10\t\n11\t1. Typed content: all copy lives in TypeScript modules checked against one schema.\n12\t2. CSS-variable design tokens: five role colors per theme drive every surface.\n13\t3. An internal animation layer: the only place the two animation libraries are imported.\n14\t4. A build and deploy pipeline: Vite build, GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages.\n15\t\n16\tEverything else is conventional React composition with props flowing down.\n17\t\n18\t## Layers\n19\t\n20\tDependencies point down only. A layer may import from layers below it, never above.\n21\t\n22\t```text\n23\t+----------------------------------------------------------------------+\n24\t| app/        main.tsx, App.tsx, Providers, Page.tsx                    |\n25\t|             Page.tsx is the ONLY file that imports content data       |\n26\t+----------------------------------------------------------------------+\n27\t| sections/   Hero, About, Experience, Projects, Skills, Education,     |\n28\t|             Contact                      (props in, JSX out)          |\n29\t+----------------------------------------------------------------------+\n30\t| layout/     Container, Section, SiteHeader, MobileNav, Footer,        |\n31\t|             SkipLink                                                  |\n32\t+----------------------------------------------------------------------+\n33\t| components/ ui/ (Button, Tag, Card, Heading, Logo, ThemeToggle, Icon) |\n34\t|             motion-primitives/ (vendored source, treated as owned)    |\n35\t+----------------------------------------------------------------------+\n36\t| anim/       the internal animation layer: the only place that         |\n37\t|             imports motion/react and @react-spring/web               |\n38\t+-------------------------------+--------------------------------------+\n39\t| hooks/  lib/                  | styles/ (tokens.css, base.css,       |\n40\t| (useActiveSection, cn, a11y)  |  index.css = tailwind + theme map)   |\n41\t+-------------------------------+--------------------------------------+\n42\t| content/ (typed TS data)      assets/ (images, fonts via Fontsource) |\n43\t+----------------------------------------------------------------------+\n44\tBuild and deploy: vite.config.ts, lint boundary rules, GitHub Actions\n45\t```\n46\t\n47\t## Import rules\n48\t\n49\tOnly src/anim/ and src/components/motion-primitives/ may import motion/react or @react-spring/web.\n50\t\n51\tOnly src/app/Page.tsx imports content data.\n52\t\n53\t| Importer | May import | May not import |\n54\t|----------|-----------|----------------|\n55\t| sections/* | layout, components/ui, the anim barrel (src/anim/index.ts), content types (not data) | motion/react, It is written so the scaffold can be built directly from it. Decisions with a longer rationale live in the [ADR log](adr/README.md).\n\n## Overview\n\nThe site is a static, zero-backend, single-page React app served from GitHub Pages. There is no router, no global store and no data fetching. The architecture comes down to four seams:\n\n1. Typed content: all copy lives in TypeScript modules checked against one schema.\n2. CSS-variable design tokens: five role colors per theme drive every surface.\n3. An internal animation layer: the only place the two animation libraries are imported.\n4. A build and deploy pipeline: Vite build, GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages.\n\nEverything else is conventional React composition with props flowing down.\n\n## Layers\n\nDependencies point down only. A layer may import from layers below it, never above.\n\n```text\n+----------------------------------------------------------------------+\n| app/        main.tsx, App.tsx, Providers, Page.tsx source, treated as owned)    |\n+----------------------------------------------------------------------+\n| anim/       the internal animation layer: the only place that         |\n|             imports motion/react and @react-spring/web               |\n+-------------------------------+--------------------------------------+\n| hooks/  lib/                  | styles/ (tokens.css, base.css,       |\n| (useActiveSection, cn, a11y)  |  index.css = tailwind + theme map)   |\n+-------------------------------+--------------------------------------+\n| content/ (typed TS data)      assets/ |\n|----------|-----------|----------------|\n| sections/* | layout, components/ui, the anim barrel (src/anim/index.ts), content types (not data) | motion/react, @react-spring/*, sections --props--> layout, ui\nassets/*     --(imagetools, hashed imports)--> image fields in content\n```\n\nRuntime, all client-side with no network use beyond same-origin assets:\n\n- Theme: an inline script in the document head reads localStorage, falls back to prefers-color-scheme, and sets the data-theme attribute on the html element before first paint. The theme provider in React only changes the attribute and storage on a user toggle.\n- Motion preference: the OS reduced-motion setting (plus an optional site override) feeds one hook, useMotionPreference, which configures both animation libraries and the wrapper components. See Reduced motion.\n- Scroll-spy: an IntersectionObserver over the section ids drives useActiveSection, which highlights the current section in the navigation.\n- Pointer and touch input drive react-spring values written straight to the DOM, with no React re-render per frame.\n- Project detail: a click or tap sets local state in the Projects section, which opens an overlay with focus handling.\n\nThere is no global state library. Three small contexts exist: theme, motion preference and, optionally, the active section. Everything else is props.\n\n## Content model\n\nAll types live in src/content/schema.ts:\n\n- Profile: name, tagline, bio paragraphs, optional quote, photo (ImageAsset), contacts.\n- ContactLink: kind (email, github, linkedin or instagram), label, href, whether it is external.\n- ExperienceEntry: id, role, org, optional org URL, optional logo, dates (DateRange), location, bullets, optional highlights and stack.\n- Project: id, title, context kind (personal, employer, course or hackathon) with a label, dates, stack, bullets, relatedExperienceId, featured, optional links and image.\n- EducationEntry: id, degree, school, location, dates, gpa, optional track.\n- SkillGroup: id, label, items as a string array.\n- DateRange: ISO start and end (or present) plus a display label in one normalized format.\n- ImageAsset: src, alt, width, height, optional srcset.\n\nRules:\n\n- Content modules use satisfies against the schema so a missing field fails typecheck.\n- Ordering lives in the data (array order or a priority field), never in components.\n- Copy is taken verbatim from the reviewed content inventory; any edit is recorded there with before and after, not made silently in code.\n- The featured flag decides what appears first on mobile, so \"key info in seconds\" is a data decision.\n- Content tests check that ids are unique, related ids resolve, every image has alt text, every external link is https, and dates parse in descending order.\n- A phone number is not a field anywhere in the model, and must never appear in site copy, metadata or the served resume.\n\n## Design tokens\n\n- Exactly five role tokens per theme: text, background, primary, secondary, accent. Light and dark are authored separately, not inverted.\n- Derived tokens (surface, border, muted text, link, focus ring and so on) are computed from the five roles with color-mix(in oklch, ...). A palette swap therefore edits one block and every derived value follows.\n- The theme is selected by the data-theme attribute on the html element.\n- Tailwind v4 is configured CSS-first: a custom dark variant is bound to [data-theme=dark] with @custom-variant, and an @theme inline block maps utilities to the CSS variables. There is no tailwind.config.js.\n- No raw hex values in components. Components use semantic utilities only; a CI check greps for stray hex.\n- A contrast test recomputes every text, UI and focus pair in both themes against WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and UI) and fails the build on any miss.\n- Spring and duration values that JavaScript needs are mirrored in CSS variables, with src/anim/tokens.ts as the canonical source for springs.\n\n## Animation layer\n\nsrc/anim/index.ts is the only animation import path for the rest of the app. It exposes a handful of semantic components and hooks, not library primitives.\n\n| Interaction class | Owner |\n|-------------------|-------|\n| Mount and unmount, presence, exit animations | motion |\n| Layout and shared-element transitions | motion |\n| Scroll-linked values and in-view reveals | motion |\n| Text and number effects, stagger, ready-made motion-primitives prefabs | motion |\n| Velocity-carrying physics: press-squish, rail hover lift with neighbor shift, theme toggle thumb | react-spring |\n| Color and hover transitions, native scroll-snap rail swipe | CSS |\n| Desktop wheel smoothing only | Lenis |\n\nThe rule: one library animates any given element. Never both libraries on one element or one property, and no Tailwind transition utilities on an element a library animates. If a vendored primitive duplicates a physics wrapper, one implementation is chosen per interaction and the other stays unused.\n\nSpring and duration tokens are defined once in src/anim/tokens.ts, exported in both libraries' formats (motion's stiffness and damping, react-spring's tension and friction), so the two feel like one system. Fine-pointer effects such as tilt, magnetic pull and spotlight are gated by (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine); touch gets a tap or press equivalent, or nothing. Every wrapper reads the motion preference, renders an instant equivalent when reduced, forwards className, and never hides content in its initial CSS state.\n\n## Reduced motion\n\nOne preference source, useMotionPreference, combines the OS prefers-reduced-motion setting with an optional site override and feeds three consumers:\n\n- motion: the provider renders MotionConfig with its reducedMotion setting. This disables transform and layout animation but not opacity or color, so wrappers handle parallax, scroll-linked and autoplay effects explicitly.\n- react-spring: the provider calls Globals.assign({ skipAnimation }) so every spring jumps to its target; the effect cleans up on change.\n- CSS: a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) guard in base.css shortens transitions and animations and keeps scroll behavior native.\n\nContent is visible by default and is never hidden until JavaScript runs. Hidden initial states are applied client-side inside wrappers, and a noscript rule guarantees visibility. Pressed, focused and selected states must read without motion (color, outline, shape). Lenis is off under reduced motion. The provider listens for changes to the media query so a live OS toggle takes effect without a reload.\n\n## Assets\n\n- Images live in src/assets/images/ and are imported as modules (hashed, long-cached). vite-imagetools produces AVIF and WebP variants and srcset with intrinsic width and height to prevent layout shift. Below-the-fold images lazy-load; the hero image is high priority.\n- Fonts are self-hosted through Fontsource (variable, latin subset, font-display swap), at most two families. No third-party font CDN.\n- Brand icons (GitHub, LinkedIn, Instagram, email) are inline SVG, because the UI icon set has no brand glyphs. See the ADR log.\n- The resume PDF served from public/ is a phone-number-free copy of the source resume.\n- Only images that are actually used migrate from the previous site, with EXIF metadata stripped. Template leftovers are left behind.\n\n## Build and deploy\n\nGitHub Actions builds the site and publishes it to GitHub Pages. The Vite base comes from the VITE_BASE environment variable: the project URL path (for example /aa-phan-portfolio-v2/) while staging, and / after the cutover to the user-site URL. The cutover checklist and rollback are not yet rehearsed.\n\nHow the site is built, deployed to a staging project URL, cut over to the user-site URL and rolled back. The reasoning is in [ADR-0003](adr/0003-github-pages-source-and-cutover.md); the build-side design is in [architecture.md](architecture.md).\n\n## Environments\n\n| Environment | URL | VITE_BASE |\n|-------------|-----|-----------|\n| Staging (project site of this repo) | https://aa-phan.github.io/aa-phan-portfolio-v2/ | /aa-phan-portfolio-v2/ |\n| Production (user site) | https://aa-phan.github.io/ | / |\n\nAssets are module-imported, so no absolute asset paths exist. Anything under `public/` that JavaScript references goes through `import.meta.env.BASE_URL`.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n1. OD-01 resolved (2026-10-09): the owner's personal contact details were rewritten out of this repo's entire history. Before any push, run both guards; each must print nothing except the known false positives below.\n\n   ```sh\n   # Bytes, not characters, so the multi-byte separators match in any locale.\n   export LC_ALL=C\n   SEP=$'([-./ \\t]|\\xc2[\\xa0\\xad]|\\xe2\\x80[\\x80-\\x8a\\x90-\\x95\\xaf]|\\xe2\\x81\\x9f|\\xe2\\x88\\x92|\\xe3\\x80\\x80)'\n   PAT=\"[0-9]{3}(${SEP}|\\\\))+[0-9]{3}(${SEP})+[0-9]{4}\"\n   ```\n\n   - History guard: `git log --all -E -G\"$PAT\" --oneline`\n   - Tree guard (file names only, never the digits): `git grep -lE \"$PAT\" HEAD`\n\n   The separator set is the same as `scripts/check-no-phone.mjs` for literal characters: hyphen, dot, slash, space, tab, no-break and soft hyphen, the Unicode spaces U+2000 to U+200A, hyphens and dashes U+2010 to U+2015, narrow no-break space, medium mathematical space, minus sign and ideographic space. A closing parenthesis is also allowed between the first two groups, for `(area) exchange`. The guard differs from the script in what it does not read: HTML entities and `\\uXXXX` escapes (the script decodes both), and contiguous digit runs, which the script checks in string literals and markup but a plain-text grep over source would flood with hashes and ids. It also reads source and docs, not the built output.\n\n   Known false positives (owner decision, 2026-10-26); any other hit stops the push:\n   - Commit `4517011` and the tree hit `.planning/phases/02-deployed-themed-skeleton/02-REVIEW-iter1.md` (the first review, renamed from `02-REVIEW.md`): its example number is all nines, not a real number.\n   - Commit `b56e593` and the tree hit `.planning/phases/01-decisions-and-documentation/01-07-PLAN.md`: a shell loop over three viewport widths, which the space separator added to the guard now matches.\n   - Wireframe viewport widths written as three numbers joined by slashes (\"wireframes at\" a phone, tablet and desktop width), which the slash separator added to the guard matches. Commits `c22f07b`, `b2f8b04`, `b56e593`, `991c252`, `d01324e` and `dd50558`, and the tree hits `.planning/ROADMAP.md`, `.planning/research/ARCHITECTURE.md` and, under `.planning/phases/01-decisions-and-documentation/`, `01-01-PLAN.md`, `01-01-SUMMARY.md` and `01-CONTEXT.md`.\n2. Node 22.12 or newer locally, `lts/*` in CI.\n3. A committed lockfile (`npm ci` fails without one).\n4. The Pages source set to GitHub Actions on the deploying repository.\n5. `gh` authenticated, for the checks below.\n\n## Workflows\n\nEvery action is pinned by commit SHA with its version in a comment.\n\n**ci.yml**, on `push` and `pull_request` (concurrency per ref, permissions `contents: read`, `VITE_BASE=/aa-phan-portfolio-v2/`), one job on `ubuntu-latest`:\n\n1. `actions/checkout` v7.0.1\n2. `actions/setup-node` v7.1.0 with `lts/*` and the npm cache\n3. `npm ci`\n4. `npm run verify`, which runs in order: typecheck, lint (includes the import-boundary rules), format check, unit tests, path-case check on the Linux runner, raw-color check, contrast check, build, initial JavaScript budget (the build fails if initial JS exceeds 150 kB gzipped), phone-number check over the built output\n5. `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`\n6. `npm run test:e2e` (builds, then runs the Playwright suite against the preview server)\n\n**deploy.yml** (\"Deploy static content to Pages\"), on `push` to `main` and on `workflow_dispatch`, following the Vite static-deploy guide:\n\n- Permissions: workflow default `contents: read`; the build job adds `pages: read` (for `configure-pages`); only the deploy job gets `pages: write` and `id-token: write`.\n- Concurrency group `pages` with `cancel-in-progress: false`, so a running deploy is never cut off.\n- e2e job: `actions/checkout` v7.0.1, `actions/setup-node` v7.1.0, `npm ci`, `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`, `npm run test:e2e`. It runs on its own because the browser download is not covered by the lockfile or the SHA pins, and it holds no Pages permissions.\n- Build job (after e2e): `actions/checkout`, `actions/setup-node`, `npm ci`, `npm run verify` (so a build that fails any gate, including the JavaScript budget and the phone check, is never deployed), `actions/configure-pages` v6.0.0, then `actions/upload-pages-artifact` v5.0.0 with path `./dist`. The uploaded `dist` is the one the gates scanned. `VITE_BASE` is set in the workflow `env`; the cutover changes it to `/`.\n- Deploy job: `actions/deploy-pages` v5.0.1, in environment `github-pages`, followed by a `curl` check that the deployed page contains the owner's name.\n\nThe phone check reads PDF text drawn from compressed (Flate) content streams. Text in uncompressed streams and text set in CID or custom-encoded fonts is not read, so the real resume PDF also gets a manual look for a phone number before it replaces the stand-in.\n\n## First staging deploy\n\nWhat actually happened on 2026-10-18:\n\n1. The repository `aa-phan-portfolio-v2` already existed and was public, with `main` pushed, before the scaffold milestone. The create-repository step was therefore already done.\n2. The history and tree guards from Prerequisites were run over every local commit, every public branch and tag, the working tree and the public `main` tip. Every one printed nothing.\n3. The owner set Pages, Source, to GitHub Actions in the repository settings before the push, so the first deploy did not fail in `configure-pages`.\n4. `main` was pushed normally (never forced). The first deploy ran from that push; no manual `workflow_dispatch` was needed.\n5. The staging URL https://aa-phan.github.io/aa-phan-portfolio-v2/ served the hero with every asset under `/aa-phan-portfolio-v2/`, and the full Playwright suite passed against it (see Local verification).\n6. The real-device [smoke test](#smoke-test) is run by the owner on a phone.\n\nTo repeat it on a fresh repository: stop unless the Prerequisites guard prints nothing, create the repository, set Pages, Source, to GitHub Actions, push `main`, and watch both workflows.\n\n## Local verification\n\n- `npm run verify` runs every gate that CI runs, except the end-to-end suite. Use `VITE_BASE=/aa-phan-portfolio-v2/` to match staging.\n- `npm run test:e2e` builds and runs the Playwright suite against a local server.\n- To check a live deployment, set `E2E_BASE_URL` to its URL and run `npx playwright test`; no local server starts in that mode. For staging: `E2E_BASE_URL=https://aa-phan.github.io/aa-phan-portfolio-v2/ npx playwright test`.\n\n## Cutover checklist\n\nImplements the cutover decisions in ADR-0003. Do it in one sitting. The live site is the iPod site until the last steps.\n\n1. Confirm staging passes the smoke test and the owner has approved it.\n2. Clone `aa-phan/aa-phan.github.io` fresh into an empty directory.\n3. Tag the current site and push the tag: `git tag v1-ipod` then `git push origin v1-ipod`.\n4. Push a matching branch from the tagged commit: `git push origin v1-ipod:refs/heads/v1-ipod`.\n5. Create a working branch, for example `cutover`.\n6. Remove the iPod files with `git rm`.\n7. Copy in the new site source and its workflow files. Do not copy private planning files or the private reference folder.\n8. Commit, push the working branch and open a pull request into `main`.\n9. Check that CI passes on the pull request, then merge it. The history stays additive.\n10. In the same sitting, set Pages, Source, to GitHub Actions on `aa-phan.github.io`.\n11. Run the deploy workflow with `workflow_dispatch` and watch the run to completion.\n12. Run the [smoke test](#smoke-test) against https://aa-phan.github.io/. If anything fails, go to [Rollback](#rollback).\n\n## Smoke test\n\nAgainst the URL being tested:\n\n- The URL loads and the hero is visible.\n- Every asset returns 200 (no 404s in the network panel).\n- The theme toggle switches between light and dark and the choice survives a reload.\n- The resume download works.\n- Copy email works and gives visible confirmation.\n- No errors in the console.\n- A mobile viewport check: layout holds at phone width, the project rail scrolls by touch, and tap targets are reachable.\n\n## Rollback\n\nIf the new site is broken after the cutover:\n\n1. In the `aa-phan.github.io` settings, set Pages, Source, back to \"Deploy from a branch\", branch `main`, folder `/`.\n2. Run `git revert` on the cutover merge commit (use `-m 1` for a merge commit), push it through a pull request or directly to `main`, and wait for the legacy build to publish.\n3. Or restore the old site from the tag with a normal commit: check out the files from `v1-ipod` (`git checkout v1-ipod -- .`), commit and push.\n4. Never force-push `aa-phan.github.io`, for the rollback or for anything else.\n5. Re-run the smoke test against https://aa-phan.github.io/ to confirm the iPod site is back.\n\n## Known risks\n\n- The Pages source switch may cause a short 404 window. This is unverified (OD-05). The path-case check exists for this.\n- A stale CDN cache can serve the old site for a few minutes after a deploy. Hard-refresh or add a query string before concluding a deploy failed.\n- A missing lockfile makes `npm ci` fail in both workflows.\n- A lockfile generated on macOS can lack the optional native bindings Linux needs.
